title: Crate reachability census: announce loudly every crate with zero callers and no runtime trigger
description:
WHAT: extend the kernel-baked census from GATES to EVERY CRATE. Josh, standing requirement: "every crate with zero callers needs to be announced loudly." The supervisor must refuse to report healthy while any crate has neither a manifest caller nor a runtime trigger on the machine it runs on.

MEASURED 2026-08-31 via `cargo metadata --no-deps` reverse edges (NOT grep -- grep is unusable here: a census that greps crate names matches its own table, the self-referential-checker defect that hit six times today):

  20 workspace crates. SIX have manifest callers:
    ack-stage <- omp-orchestrator | finding <- finding-dispatch | omp-orchestrator <- finding-dispatch
    receiver-receipt <- ack-stage, omp-orchestrator | subprocess-contract <- finding, omp-orchestrator, pane-dispatch-fence
    tick-monitor <- ack-stage, receiver-receipt
  FOURTEEN have ZERO manifest callers. Split by whether that is expected:

  TWO LIBRARIES WITH ZERO CALLERS -- unambiguously dead, no runtime excuse available:
    finding-dispatch      (and note: it is omp-orchestrator's ONLY manifest caller, so the supervisor's sole inbound edge is itself dead code)
    path-literal-guard

  TWELVE BINS -- a bin's caller is a runtime trigger, so these were checked against git hooks, launchd, crontab, and ~/.local/bin:
    TRIGGERED (2):   no-shell-gate (.git/hooks/pre-commit, PROVEN to refuse a staged .sh at exit 1)
                     fleet-composite (crontab)
    INSTALLED BUT NO TRIGGER (3):  composer-typed, loop-queue-filter, pane-dispatch-fence
    NO TRIGGER AND NOT INSTALLED (7): ack-spine, dispatch-silence-watch, kernel-bypass-gate,
                     kernel-only-operator-hook, pre-delete-citation-check, state-wildcard-lint,
                     undrained-pipe-lint

  TOTAL WITH NO PATH TO EXECUTION: 12 of 20.

WHY: this is the third rule generalised. A crate that cannot run reads as capability and is not. Every gap in today's reality check was an instance -- the flagship gate wired to a workflow with no remote, authorities.rs green via a #[path] private copy while the library never compiled it, ledger.rs byte-identical and inert, ATTENTION.txt 178 ticks with one writer and zero readers, the supervisor's typed refusal unread 29 times, dispatch-actuation retired for having no inbound edge, and `finding` -- built so a named gap would be an obligation -- shipped with zero callers, which made it an unfiled gap about unfiled gaps.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. TWO AXES, REPORTED SEPARATELY: manifest reachability (from cargo metadata edges, never grep) and runtime trigger (git hooks, launchd, crontab, installed binaries). A lib with no manifest caller is DEAD. A bin with no manifest caller is EXPECTED but needs a named trigger; with neither it is DARK.
2. LOUD MEANS A TYPED NONZERO REFUSAL, not a log line. Measured: ATTENTION.txt got 178 consecutive ticks from one writer with zero readers, and the supervisor printed a typed refusal naming owner=josh 29 times unread. The only signal that reached a human today was a nonzero outcome the operator had to answer. Reuse the GateUnwired mechanism: CrateUnreachable { crate, axis, detail }, checked in decide() before any healthy verdict.
3. POSITIVE CONTROL, mandatory: subprocess-contract (3 manifest callers) must report REACHABLE and no-shell-gate must report TRIGGERED. A census that flags everything is indistinguishable from a broken one.
4. EXCLUDE THE CENSUS'S OWN SOURCE. Sixth self-referential instance today: a shell census reported all six gates as having callers because the census table named them all.
5. ANTI-VACUITY: zero crates discovered is an ERROR, never a pass.
6. ALLOWLIST STARTS EMPTY, entries carry a reason -- the AGENTS.md UNWIRED_LANE_ALLOWANCE shape, where an exception is a named row, not silence.
7. MUTATION: add a crate with no callers; the leg goes RED and NAMES it. Restore byte-identically, sha both sides.

NO-CLAIM: manifest edges and installed triggers prove a path EXISTS, never that it RAN. tick-monitor has 2 manifest callers and a live process and still starved the fleet for 4.5 hours. Runtime witness is a separate question. Also machine-scoped: .git/hooks is per-clone and untracked, so a fresh checkout reports no-shell-gate as DARK, and the census must say which machine it answered for.

ADDED ACCEPTANCE CLAUSE — EVERY CRATE DECLARES THE OMP SURFACE IT MAPS TO:
The census gains a THIRD AXIS beside manifest reachability and runtime trigger: the OMP surface declaration. Each crate row answers "which of OMP's 57 type-surface directories / 39 CLI subcommands / --mode=rpc transport does this crate map to?" with one of:
  (a) NONE, genuinely not OMP's concern -- a legitimate terminal state, reachable without argument.
      Worked example: no-shell-gate is a repo gate over our own tree and correctly maps to nothing.
  (b) REIMPLEMENTED BY SCRAPING -- names the OMP surface AND the alternative that exists today.
      Four are already classified this way by two independent measurements: pane state, dispatch,
      session, health check.
  (c) UNUSED CAPABILITY we should adopt. Five already classified: muxConnect, muxPing,
      muxRestartServer, goals, collab.
  UNDECLARED -- and this is the new failure state. A crate with no declaration is FLAGGED, exactly
  as a crate with no caller is flagged. Silence is not category (a); (a) is a stated answer.

WHY THIS BELONGS HERE RATHER THAN IN A NEW BEAD: you already compute the two hardest axes. A separate crate recomputing the same reverse edges would drift from this one, and this session has measured what drift costs -- a fixture drifted from production certifies nothing, because its green is indistinguishable from a working check.

THE TRAP THAT WILL BITE THIS SPECIFICALLY: do not infer the declaration by grepping crate sources for OMP surface names. A census that greps names matches its own table -- the self-referential checker, SIX instances in one session, and it produced a reading where all six gates falsely appeared to have callers. The declaration must be DECLARED, in the crate's own manifest or a checked-in table, not inferred.

POSITIVE CONTROL for the new axis: at least one crate must come back with a non-UNDECLARED value, or the axis is broken and every UNDECLARED is suspect. no-shell-gate is the natural control -- its answer is (a) and it is defensible.

NO-CLAIM: a declaration is a CLAIM BY THE AUTHOR, not a measurement. A crate can declare (a) and be wrong. The census's job is to make the claim EXIST and be visible for challenge, not to adjudicate it. Adjudication is the inventory map's four-field discipline (inputs, outputs, what must be true, negative evidence) on bead omp-coverage-mission-ipg.12.

title: tick-monitor scored a pane blocked on an Ask dialog as WORKING/LIVE
description:
WHAT: on OMP v18 an Ask/approval dialog renders ABOVE the status line, and the status line remains LAST with an advancing spinner and timer. `classify` therefore scored a pane blocked on a human answer as `Working`, and `liveness` scored it `Live` indefinitely -- because the timer really does advance while the pane waits. A pane awaiting an answer was indistinguishable from a pane doing work.

HOW IT WAS FOUND: dogfooding, 2026-08-31 ~11:30Z. The operator reported the OPPOSITE polarity -- their own watcher scored %1413 GONE at 09:15Z on an Ask dialog, and specified the defect as 'dialog covers the status line -> classifier finds no model line -> Unproven -> dropped from capacity'. I went to reproduce that on a live pane and it DID NOT reproduce: %1372 had a dialog open and its last line was ' 26m . GPT-5.6-Luna . ~/Developer/control-plane', a perfectly readable status line. `last_status_line` returned it, spinner+timer matched, and the pane scored WORKING. So the specified failure was not mine; the real one was the same class as `Wedged` -- LOOKS BUSY, IS NOT -- and it was hiding a real escalation: %1372 sat 36 minutes on the arc-keepalive install approval reading as healthy work.

MEASURED IMPACT: the pane the whole fleet was waiting on (the gated binary install escalated to Joshua) was invisible to the conductor because it looked productive. A conductor polling for idle capacity would never surface it, and a conductor watching for frozen panes would never surface it either, because the timer was genuinely moving.

THE FIX (76bef30):
1. `PaneState::Dialog { timer_secs }` and `Liveness::Dialog { timer_secs }` -- ALIVE, NOT dispatchable, NOT free capacity, plus a new `needs_answer()` predicate. Answering is the action, not filling, so it is deliberately NOT folded into `is_free_capacity`.
2. `dialog_open()` is POSITIONAL, not shape-based. First attempt keyed on `line is box-framed AND contains a footer marker`. THAT SELF-POLLUTED: my own pane carries box-framed lines containing 'Esc cancel' because OMP renders tool-call blocks inside frames and my commands quoted the marker. Measured: 4 unframed + 3 framed matches in my own scrollback. The discriminator that survives is ADJACENCY -- the footer must sit within the three non-blank lines immediately above the status line. Same lesson as `in_citation_position` and as `last_status_line` anchoring on the LAST line: shape alone is not enough, because a dialog's text is shaped like content.
3. Checked BEFORE the spinner branch, like `Wedged`. Order is load-bearing: a dialog pane HAS a live spinner, so a spinner-first check scores it WORKING.
4. `vanished(prior, live_ids)` -- the ONLY death authority is absence from `tmux list-panes`. It returns EMPTY for an empty live list, because a failed scan must never produce a fleet-wide obituary.

TWO FURTHER BUGS THE TESTS CAUGHT, both the same `_ => 0` catch-all class:
- `save()` wrote `timer_secs: 0` for DIALOG, so the state file round-tripped the variant but lost the timer. Caught by the round-trip leg, not by review.
- `main.rs`'s JSON renderer had the SAME catch-all in a second place. The round-trip test could not see it because it never renders JSON. Caught only by comparing the live run (`timer_secs=0`) against the pane's own status line (which plainly read `35m`). Both now spell every variant explicitly; there is no wildcard left to absorb the next state.

ACCEPTANCE -- 49 tests + 44 selftest legs, and the gate BITES:
- planted VERBATIM live dialog capture (tests/fixtures/dialog_v18.txt, captured from %1372) -> asserts label 'DIALOG', not 'WORKING'
- planted normal working capture -> 'WORKING'; planted idle -> 'IDLE' (the new state does not swallow the old ones)
- planted SELF-POLLUTION capture: framed marker far from the status line -> NOT a dialog, and classifies 'WORKING'
- planted absent pane id -> reported dead; a pane WITH a dialog open in the same call -> NOT dead (asserting both in one test is what proves they are distinguished rather than merged)
- planted empty pane list -> nobody dead (anti-vacuity)
- Dialog is !is_dispatchable, !is_free_capacity, needs_answer
- state-file round trip preserves Dialog{timer_secs}
Every leg asserts a SPECIFIC state name. None asserts merely 'did not crash'.

MUTATION, both restored byte-identically (sha256 4a665ddff49a7010 before and after):
- delete the dialog branch from `classify` -> `planted_dialog_is_dialog_not_working` FAILED
- widen adjacency from 3 lines to the whole buffer -> `framed_marker_far_from_status_line_is_not_a_dialog` FAILED
So the detector and its narrowing are each independently attributable.

LIVE PROOF: `tick-monitor observe --session ''` now reports `%1372 DIALOG timer_secs=2160 liveness=DIALOG`, dispatchable=[], free_capacity=[]. Before the fix that pane reported WORKING/LIVE.

COMPILER AS A GATE, worth recording: adding the variant broke the exhaustive `(prev, now)` match with E0004 -- exactly as that match's comment promises ('If a new PaneState is added, this match must fail to compile rather than absorb it into Live'). The wildcard-free design caught a real omission at build time; the `_ => 0` catch-alls in `save` and the renderer, which were NOT wildcard-free, both shipped the bug.

NO-CLAIM -- what this classifier still cannot see:
- It recognises the dialog FOOTER strings measured on OMP v18 ('Enter select', 'Esc cancel', up/down move) inside a framed line adjacent to the status line. A dialog rendered WITHOUT those markers, or with the footer more than three non-blank lines above the status line, still reads WORKING. The marker list is a hand-maintained list mirroring a real set, which is the exact drift class fh C75 warns about.
- MODEL_MARKERS is likewise hand-maintained ('Opus 5', 'GLM 5.3', 'GPT-5.6', 'GPT-5.5'). A new model name makes `dialog_open` return false and the pane fall back to spinner classification -- fail-toward-WORKING, which is the wrong direction for this specific bug.
- It does not measure how long the DIALOG has been open. `timer_secs` is the pane's TURN timer, which was already running before the dialog appeared; it is an upper bound on dialog age, not the age.
- `vanished()` is a pure function and IS unit-tested, but it is NOT yet called from the observe path -- so tick-monitor still does not report DEAD in production. That is a BUILT != WIRED gap I am naming rather than leaving for a reader to discover, and it is the next thing to close.
- The operator's ORIGINAL specified defect (status line genuinely covered -> no model line found) is NOT fixed and NOT reproduced here; if some dialog shape does cover the status line, `classify` returns `Unproven`, which is fail-safe (excluded from capacity) but still reports the wrong reason. No capture of that shape exists in this repo to plant.

comments.author: josh
comments.text:
WIRED + OBSCURED (933c2eb) -- closing my own BUILT != WIRED gap, and correcting the fail-safe excuse I offered for the covered-status-line case.

=== 1. vanished() NOW HAS A NAMED PRODUCTION CALLER ===
crates/tick-monitor/src/main.rs:202, inside `observe_core`:
    let dead = tick_monitor::vanished(&prior.panes, &ids);
Rendered at main.rs:314 as `"dead_panes":{"ids":[...],"count":N}`. A value computed and never printed is still unwired, so the render is part of the wiring, not a nicety.

Ordering matters and is asserted by construction: the call sits AFTER the two existing refusals -- `pane_ids` returns Err on a tmux timeout (a timeout is not an empty fleet) and observe refuses an empty pane set outright -- and `vanished` independently returns empty for an empty list. Three independent guards, because the failure mode here is a fleet-wide obituary generated from a failed scan.

WIRING PROOF, and it bites: `vanished_has_a_production_caller_in_the_binary` reads main.rs and asserts the call site plus both rendered fields, WITH a positive control asserting the scan can report absence (a grep that can never miss is not evidence -- fh N043 is this repo failing exactly that way). MUTATION: replaced the call with `let dead: Vec<String> = Vec::new();` -> test FAILED; restored, green. NO-CLAIM on its class: this is a SOURCE-level check, the same mechanism no-shell-gate's wired_lanes uses. It proves a call site EXISTS in the production binary; it does not prove that site executes. That is the live run below, and it is a different kind of evidence.

LIVE PROOF, planted known-bad + real positive, all 34 panes of this box:
  tick 1 seeded 34 panes into a scratch state file
  injected `pane\t%99999\tWORKING\t120\t7\t1788170000` -- a pane id that does not exist
  tick 2 -> dead_panes {"ids":["%99999"],"count":1}
           attention  {"panes":["%1372:DIALOG"],"count":1}
           dispatchable []
The planted absent id is reported dead; the REAL dialog pane, present in tmux, is NOT reported dead and instead lands in attention. Both halves in one run, which is what proves DEAD and DIALOG are distinguished rather than merged.

=== 2. THE COVERED STATUS LINE: I WAS WRONG THAT FAIL-SAFE WAS ENOUGH ===
I wrote 'classify returns Unproven -- fail-safe but wrong reason'. The operator's correction is right and it is not stylistic: Unproven is DROPPED FROM CAPACITY, and dropping is precisely how a live pane goes untended. Their watcher scored %1413 GONE at 09:15Z on this shape.

But their FIX is also not right, and they said so: after it, it produced a FALSE DIALOG on %1414 at 09:38Z when a box-drawing region briefly covered a pane mid-work at 26/26. So the third state must NOT be Dialog. A covered status line is an OBSERVATION failure; a dialog is a pane WAITING FOR AN ANSWER. Inferring the second from evidence for the first invents a blocker that does not exist -- and a conductor that believes a working pane is waiting on it will interrupt real work.

THE DISCRIMINATOR IS THE PRIOR OBSERVATION, NOT THE SHAPE OF THIS CAPTURE. A pane that carried a model-name line last tick and carries none now is alive and OBSCURED. A pane that never carried one is a shell. This reuses the crate's existing two-capture mechanism rather than adding a new heuristic, and it cannot produce the %1414 false positive: that pane's prior state was Working, so it reads OBSCURED (attention: LOOK), never DIALOG (attention: ANSWER).

IMPLEMENTATION: `Liveness::Obscured` -- !is_dispatchable, !is_free_capacity, !needs_answer, needs_attention. The now-Unproven check MOVED from above the `prev` resolution to below it, so the prior state is available; and `pane_id_mismatch` was moved ABOVE it, because comparing a prior observation from a DIFFERENT pane is not evidence about this one. `needs_attention()` is deliberately NOT filtered by --exclude-pane: the conductor's own pane can be obscured or prompting too, and 'not worker capacity' is not 'need not look'.

FIXTURE PLANTED -- the thing I previously said I could not plant. I wrote 'no capture of that shape exists in this repo to plant' and left the behaviour untested. Synthesised it instead: `COVERED`, a box-drawing region occupying the last lines with NO dialog footer. Five legs, each asserting a SPECIFIC name:
  a_covered_status_line_is_not_a_dialog          -> dialog_open false, classify UNPROVEN
  a_covered_pane_that_was_working_is_obscured    -> OBSCURED, needs_attention, !dispatchable, !needs_answer
  a_shell_pane_stays_unproven_and_is_never_obscured -> UNPROVEN (prior Unproven)
  a_covered_pane_with_no_prior_is_unproven       -> UNPROVEN (one capture is not a liveness claim)
  a_dialog_still_beats_a_covered_frame           -> DIALOG survives; OBSCURED does not swallow it

MUTATION, both restored byte-identically (sha256 d6299265c5e13b84 before and after):
  A: Obscured arm -> Unproven  -> a_covered_pane_that_was_working_is_obscured_not_dropped FAILED
  B: fire Obscured regardless of prior -> a_shell_pane_stays_unproven_and_is_never_obscured FAILED
So the state AND its prior-state discriminator are each independently attributable. Leg B is the one that matters: without it, 'no model line -> alive and obscured' would relabel every shell pane as a live agent needing attention and the attention list would be permanently noisy -- an over-strict gate, which gets routed around.

STANDING: 56 tests (22 lib + 34 integration) + 44 selftest legs, all green.

NO-CLAIM, updated:
- OBSCURED requires a PRIOR observation. On a cold start every covered pane reads UNPROVEN and is still dropped for exactly one tick. That is deliberate -- one capture is not a liveness claim -- but it is a real hole with a named duration.
- DIALOG_FOOTER and MODEL_MARKERS remain hand-maintained lists mirroring a real set (fh C75 drift class). A new model name makes `dialog_open` return false AND makes OBSCURED impossible to reach for that pane, because its prior would never be model-bearing either. The two failure modes compound rather than cancelling.
- `dead_panes` is now reported. Nothing ACTS on it -- no respawn, no bead, no escalation. It is an observation surface, and calling it 'death handling' would be the same overclaim I am closing here.
- The live proof used an INJECTED pane id, not an organically dead pane. It proves the code path fires on an absent id; it does not prove behaviour during a real pane teardown race, where the pane may vanish between `list-panes` and `capture-pane`.
- I did not re-verify the operator's %1413/%1414 measurements; they are cited as reported. My legs are planted against synthesised and verbatim-captured shapes in this repo.

title: Dispatch refuses a packet naming an unclaimed bead — enforce the middle beat in code
description:
WHAT: the dispatch path must REFUSE to send a packet naming a bead that is not `in_progress` and assigned to the receiving agent. File -> CLAIM -> dispatch, with the middle beat enforced by the code rather than remembered by the conductor.

WHY, measured 2026-08-31: `5rh` was dispatched to %1413 and never claimed. The bead sat `open`, `assignee: none`, ZERO comments, while a worker was actively carrying it. Silent in both directions -- the pane read as idle-with-no-assignment, and the queue read as still having ready work nobody had taken.

THE PART THAT MAKES THIS P0 RATHER THAN BOOKKEEPING: it defeats the follow-up detector we shipped today. `classify_followup` keys on (assigned + in_progress + no comment since dispatch). An unclaimed dispatch produces NO SIGNAL AT ALL -- the stage built to catch dispatched-then-silent is structurally blind to a dispatch that never became tracker state. The bead's status is a PROJECTION of the dispatch; when the projection is never written, the watcher watches an empty slot. That is the same shape as every other failure catalogued today: a mechanism that is correct and looking in a place where the event does not arrive.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. FIRES-ON-KNOWN-BAD: attempt a dispatch naming a bead that is `open`/unassigned -> REFUSED, with the bead id and its actual status in the refusal text. A refusal that does not name the bead sends the caller hunting.
2. FIRES-ON-KNOWN-BAD, second form: attempt a dispatch naming a bead assigned to a DIFFERENT agent -> REFUSED. Two panes working one bead is the duplicate-work failure, and it nearly happened today when `br ready` offered a bead an agent had been building for 14 minutes while the tracker still read `unclaimed`.
3. KNOWN-GOOD, mandatory: a correctly filed-claimed-dispatched packet passes untouched. A refuse-only gate is over-strict, gets routed around, and dies slower than no gate.
4. THE REFUSAL MUST BE ACTIONABLE, not just typed: name the exact `br update <id> --assignee <agent> --status in_progress` that would satisfy it. Measured today -- a supervisor emitted `DISPATCH_RETRY_BLOCKED owner=josh next_action=inspect-or-clear-pending-dispatch` 29 times and it worked precisely because it named the owner and the action.
5. ANTI-VACUITY: a dispatch with no bead id is an ERROR, never an unchecked pass. Broadcasts and corrections are a DIFFERENT operation and must be named as such rather than slipping through as bead-less dispatches.
6. MUTATION: remove the status check; leg 1 goes RED. Restore byte-identically, report the sha both sides.

NO-CLAIM: claiming makes work VISIBLE, not DONE. A claimed bead with a silent pane is still a silent pane -- this closes the blind spot in the detector, not the silence itself. And `open`+unassigned is NOT by itself evidence of a skipped claim: it may simply be unstarted work. The discriminating signal is DISPATCHED-and-unclaimed, which means the DISPATCH LEDGER is the authority here, not the bead. A gate reading only bead status can prove the claim exists; only the ledger can prove a dispatch happened without one.

title: Build the FOLLOW-UP stage: nothing notices dispatched-then-silent
description:
WHAT: detect a bead dispatched and then silent. Inputs bead id, assignee, dispatch timestamp, current state. Output VERDICT_POSTED, SILENT_PAST_DEADLINE, or REASSIGNED.
WHY: its absence cost four hand-chases tonight -- %1408, %1413, %1409, %1367 each went idle holding assigned work and only a manual question found it.
ACCEPTANCE: authority for VERDICT_POSTED is br comments <id> READ BACK, never an exit code -- br comment singular prefix-matches, errors on stderr, and EXITS 0, so an agent believed two VERDICT comments landed when neither had. A posted comment yields VERDICT_POSTED; silence past deadline yields SILENT_PAST_DEADLINE; a changed assignee yields REASSIGNED not silent; an unreadable tracker is an ERROR never VERDICT_POSTED. Assigned %1408.

FOLLOW-UP STAGE LANDED (SilverWolf, pane 5, %1409) — crates/ack-spine/src/followup.rs + tests/followup.rs, 6 tests green (all hermetic, no br subprocess).

THE CLASSIFIER: classify_followup(bead_id, assigned_to, original_assignee, comments_present, minutes_elapsed, deadline_minutes, tracker_readable) — pure, no I/O, no environment dependency. Takes pre-captured inputs, returns a typed FollowUpVerdict:
  VERDICT_POSTED — confirmed by read-back (comments_present=true)
  SILENT_PAST_DEADLINE — the bead was dispatched, the pane went idle, no verdict (the %1408/%1409 live case)
  REASSIGNED — the bead moved (re-dispatch needed, not a chase)
  TRACKER_ERROR — br failed (an ERROR, never VERDICT_POSTED)

THE DECIDING RULES (all four encoded as exhaustive match arms):
  1. !tracker_readable -> TrackerError (never VERDICT_POSTED — an unreadable tracker must not read as "healthy")
  2. assigned_to changed -> Reassigned (REASSIGNED takes priority over silence: a moved bead is not silent)
  3. comments_present -> VerdictPosted (confirmed by read-back, not by exit code)
  4. !comments_present && minutes >= deadline -> SilentPastDeadline (the 178-tick failure made actionable)

THE OUTPUT IS NOT A LOG LINE: followup_action() classifies the verdict as Healthy or NeedsFollowUp, and the NeedsFollowUp variant carries the SILENT_PAST_DEADLINE detail — so the operator must answer it, not read it.

title: Flagship no-shell gate is wired to a workflow that can never run (no git remote)
description:
WHAT: the repo's FIRST hard gate -- no tracked .sh/.py -- is invoked only from .github/workflows/gate.yml (cargo run -p no-shell-gate; cargo test -p no-shell-gate). `git remote -v` RETURNS EMPTY. There is no remote, so the workflow can NEVER EXECUTE. The gate has no runner.

MEASURED 2026-08-31: the gate binary itself is CORRECT. Run by hand it exits 1, names both offending files, and prints 'the exemption list is empty by design; there is no check.sh carve-out'. So this is not a detector defect -- the detector is right and unreachable.

WHAT IT COST, same day: two .sh files were committed into the tree the gate forbids -- scripts/ack-detector.sh (7187210, 12:36) and scripts/heartbeat-check.sh (298afbf, 11:30) -- while README.md hard gate 1 says the gate 'lands BEFORE the first crate is copied' precisely so the mess cannot accumulate. It accumulated anyway, in the repo whose ONE RULE is 'No .sh. No .py. Not in bin/, not in scripts/, not just for testing.'

WHY THIS IS THE MOST EXPENSIVE INSTANCE: AGENTS.md exists to prevent exactly this -- 'A mechanism that is written, tested, adversarially hardened, and invoked by nothing is worth zero.' This session hit BUILT != WIRED twelve times; this is the twelfth and the worst, because this gate defines the repository.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. The gate runs on a trigger THAT EXISTS ON THIS MACHINE, with no remote and no CI service. A pre-commit hook is the candidate; per hook-certification it must be Rust, asupersync-backed, cancel-correct, and registered in hooks_certified.toml. It must NOT be auto-registered -- a hook error reads as DENY and can brick every Write/Edit/Bash fleet-wide.
2. FIRES-ON-KNOWN-BAD through the real trigger, not by hand: stage a .sh, attempt the commit, assert refusal. Running the binary directly is what we already had and it did not stop anything.
3. KNOWN-GOOD, mandatory: a normal Rust-only commit is NOT refused. An over-strict commit gate gets bypassed with --no-verify and then protects nothing.
4. ANTI-VACUITY: an empty scan set is an ERROR. Zero tracked files must not read as a pass.
5. MUTATION: break the extension match, the known-bad leg goes RED; restore byte-identically and report the sha both sides.
6. THE WIRING TEST IS THE DELIVERABLE: assert a live trigger reaches the gate. AGENTS.md prescribes the shape -- an UNWIRED_LANE_ALLOWANCE that is EMPTY, where an exception is a named row with a reason, not silence.

NO-CLAIM: a pre-commit hook is bypassable with --no-verify by design. This raises the floor from 'nothing runs the gate' to 'skipping it is an explicit act'. It does not make committing shell impossible, and saying otherwise would be the overclaim this repo refuses.

title: Wave CONDUCTOR-WIRING: dispatch-silence-watch + dispatch-claim-fence into the conductor cron
description:
WHAT: the two dispatch-adjacency crates get wired into the conductor cron so the system detects silence and fences claims automatically.

DISPATCH-SILENCE-WATCH (85828bf): currently no manifest caller, no trigger. The conductor cron invokes it after every dispatch tick to check whether the work produced a verdict. The typed verdicts (VERDICT_POSTED / SILENT_PAST_DEADLINE / REASSIGNED / TRACKER_ERROR) feed back into the conductor's next tick decision.

DISPATCH-CLAIM-FENCE (bhw): a dispatch that names an unclaimed bead (no assignee in br show --json) is a thin-air packet — no audit trail, no assignee, dies with the pane. The fence refuses the packet and creates a bead for it instead.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. dispatch-silence-watch appears in crontab (or as a called step in a cron'd lane)
2. A test proves the wiring exists (reads crontab or the supervisor's Config to confirm)
3. dispatch-claim-fence compiles and its known-bad leg is green
4. NO-CLAIM: this wires the trigger; it does not prove the dispatched work is correct

title: Wave OMP-COVERAGE-WIRING: connect the eleven coverage waves to the supervisor decision loop
description:
WHAT: the eleven OMP coverage waves (plan/beads/triage/dispatch/observe/verify/memory/edit/security/io/runtime) are filed but unwired. Each wave produces crates that must be wired into the supervisor decision loop — not just built.

The coverage mission epic (omp-coverage-mission-ipg) defines the surfaces. This bead wires the OUTPUT of each wave into the supervisor's decide() function: each new gate/crate from a wave gets a census row in census_gates, so GateUnwired fires if the wave's gate loses its trigger.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. Every wave's output crate has at least one trigger (pre-commit, supervisor step, or cron)
2. The gate census includes every wave's output
3. NO-CLAIM: this wires the triggers; the waves must still produce correct code

comments.text: WAVE 3 STATUS (AmberGate, ~17:3xZ): census_gates extended to cover all 20 workspace crates (6 known gates + 14 library crates with manifest-caller grep). GateUnwired variant wired into decide() as the FIRST check — before pane and queue checks. Positive control: no-shell-gate must be reachable or the census is broken. None => GateUnwired{CENSUS_NOT_PERFORMED} (fail-closed). title: ack_detector tests are coupled to live tracker state and mutate a real closed bead
description:
WHAT: crates/ack-spine/tests/ack_detector.rs hardcodes the bead id `omp-orchestrator-nrj` at lines 11, 33 and 86. Those tests pass ONLY on a machine whose tracker already contains that bead, and every run posts `br comments add` to a REAL bead in the REAL tracker.

HOW IT WAS FOUND -- and tree-green hid it completely: I extracted `git archive HEAD` into a clean directory and ran the suite from the REPOSITORY rather than the working tree.
  working tree : ack_detector 4 passed, exit 0
  clean extract: ack_detector 1 passed, 3 FAILED, exit 101
Verbatim failures:
  genuinely_posted_comment_is_confirmed -> "br comments add must succeed: Error: Issue not found: omp-orchestrator-nrj"
  singular_verb_trap_produces_missing_ack -> "the singular-verb trap must produce Missing, got Unverifiable { bead_id: \"omp-orchestrator-nrj\", detail: \"br comments list exited Some(3): Error: Issue not found\" }"
  read_back_distinguishes_trap_from_good -> same Unverifiable shape

THE DETECTOR IS RIGHT AND THE TEST IS WRONG. Returning `Unverifiable` when the tracker cannot resolve the bead is EXACTLY what oj6.2's acceptance demands -- "An unreadable tracker is an ERROR, never 'no ack'." The extract run therefore fired the detector's anti-vacuity leg FOR REAL, unplanned, and the test asserted `Missing` against it. Do not weaken the detector to make the test pass; that would invert the leg.

TWO DEFECTS:
1. ENVIRONMENT COUPLING. README promises "install it on any of our machines". These tests cannot pass on a machine without this tracker, so vision goal 9 is false while they stand.
2. SHARED-STATE MUTATION. Every run appends a comment to `omp-orchestrator-nrj`, which is a CLOSED bead titled "GRADER-STALENESS-PROBE (deletion candidate)". The tests write to production tracker state, and they are pinned to a bead someone is expected to delete. When it is deleted the suite goes red for a reason unrelated to the code -- the same class as today's port that deleted four scripts and silently invalidated every closed bead citing them.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. HERMETIC: the tests create their own scratch tracker (temp dir + `br --db`, or a scratch bead they create and delete), assert, and clean up. No hardcoded live bead id anywhere in the file.
2. THE PROOF IS THE EXTRACT, NOT THE TREE: `git archive HEAD | tar -x -C <tmp>` then `cargo test -p ack-spine` from that directory must exit 0. Tree-green is explicitly NOT acceptance for this bead, because tree-green is the condition that hid the defect.
3. PRESERVE THE THREE-VALUED VERDICT: Missing / Confirmed / Unverifiable must remain distinct, and a test must assert Unverifiable for an unreadable tracker, since that path now has a live specimen.
4. NO WRITES TO PRODUCTION TRACKER STATE from any test. Known-bad: point the suite at the real tracker and assert it refuses rather than mutating.
5. MUTATION: re-hardcode a live bead id, leg 2 goes RED from the extract. Restore byte-identically, report the sha both sides.

NO-CLAIM: this is one crate's suite. Whether other crates' tests are environment-coupled is UNMEASURED -- the extract harness that found this can answer it, and that is a separate bead, not an assumption to fold in here.

title: Watcher reset its stall counter on idle capacity, so an idle pane never alarmed (3 incidents/shift)
description:
WHAT: the watch loop treated a freed worker as MOTION, which RESET the stall counter, so persistent idle capacity could never raise an alarm. Fixed in 228f42a; this bead records the defect, the measurement, and the grading it still owes.

THREE INCIDENTS IN ONE SHIFT, all the same shape -- the operator noticed an idle pane before I did:
  1. %1409 and %1408 idle    -- loop recorded it at ticks 6 and 7; I never read the ledger.
  2. %1413 idle              -- loop recorded it at tick 12 and reported it free at ticks 12, 13, 14, 15
                                (about six minutes). Operator: 'idle pane 2 w/o nnotice'.
  3. (the first, earlier)    -- three panes idle simultaneously; operator: '3 of your workers idle'.
Every time the detector worked and the ESCALATION did not.

ROOT CAUSE, and it is a logic inversion, not a missing feature. crates/tick-monitor/src/main.rs, watch():
    let moved = !line.contains("new_total":0)
             || !line.contains("transitions":[])
             || !line.contains("free_capacity":[]);      <-- free capacity counted as MOTION
    if moved { no_value = 0 } else { no_value += 1 }
`no_value` counts ticks where NOTHING happened, and `stall_after` alarms on that streak. But a
worker going idle IS something happening, so every idle pane RESET the counter to zero. The one
condition most worth alarming on was the one condition guaranteed to silence the alarm. A loop that
reports healthy while capacity sits unused is 'a dead loop wearing live makeup' in the exact sense
L57 names.

SECOND DEFECT FOUND WHILE FIXING IT: free_capacity included %1397 -- the ORCHESTRATOR'S OWN PANE.
Measured at ticks 14 and 15: free=['%1397','%1413']. The conductor goes idle between turns by design,
so an alarm keyed on free capacity would have fired continuously and been trained away within an hour.
This is verbatim the 'LIVENESS counting the orchestrator as a worker' defect named in
/ntm-fleet-monitor's reporting contract, reproduced by me while building the liveness monitor.

THIRD, ARCHITECTURAL, AND NOT FULLY FIXED: the ledger is append-only and grows, and nothing pushes to
the conductor. I criticised pane-truth's --selftest for only running when a human remembers, then
built a ledger that only helps when I remember to read it. Within this harness a process cannot push
to an agent session, so 228f42a's mitigation is a single-line ATTENTION.txt overwritten every tick --
cheap enough to read first, every tick. That is a mitigation, NOT a mechanism. The real mechanism is
/loop-enforcement's LLM-substrate variant (a hook injecting a system-reminder at every wake), and
installing any hook is gated by /hook-certification's six-stage gauntlet. Until that exists, this
failure mode is contained by discipline, and discipline is what already failed three times. SAY SO
rather than claiming it is solved.

WHAT 228f42a CHANGED:
  - `free_streak` counts CONSECUTIVE ticks with free capacity, independent of `no_value`.
  - `--capacity-alarm-after` (default 2) prints a loud IDLE CAPACITY line on stdout so `hub logs`
    shows it without parsing JSON. Default is 2, not 1, because one tick of free capacity is the
    healthy case -- a worker finished, and NewlyIdle needs a second capture to confirm anyway.
  - `--exclude-pane` (repeatable) removes a pane from BOTH dispatchable and free_capacity; the live
    watcher now runs with --exclude-pane %1397 --exclude-pane %1396.
  - `free_capacity_streak` is recorded on every ledger row, so the history is auditable.
  - ATTENTION.txt: one line, overwritten each tick, three states (all occupied / free seen / IDLE
    CAPACITY for N ticks).

ACCEPTANCE -- and I cannot grade this, I wrote it:
1. FIRES-ON-KNOWN-BAD, the leg that matters: construct a tick sequence where free capacity persists
   for >= capacity_alarm_after ticks and assert the alarm fires. Then assert that against the code at
   228f42a^ it does NOT fire. If it fires at the parent, the fix fixed nothing.
2. KNOWN-GOOD: a single tick of free capacity (one worker just finished) must NOT alarm. An alarm on
   the healthy case is how alarms get ignored -- that is the whole reason the default is 2.
3. The conductor's pane must never appear in free_capacity or dispatchable when excluded. Assert with
   %1397 both excluded and not excluded, so the flag is proven to do something.
4. ATTENTION.txt contains exactly one line and is overwritten, not appended -- assert its length does
   not grow across ticks. A growing 'attention' file is the ledger problem again.
5. Live proof: on a session where a pane is genuinely idle for two ticks, `cat ATTENTION.txt` says
   IDLE CAPACITY and `hub logs tick-monitor` shows the loud line. Paste both.
6. NO-CLAIM: this alarms; it does not dispatch. The monitor stays observation-only on purpose. And it
   cannot make the conductor read it -- see the third defect above. Do not close this bead claiming
   the class is eliminated; the mitigation reduces the cost of forgetting, it does not remove
   forgetting from the loop.

title: kernel-bypass gate: detects raw invocations that duplicate an existing kernel's interface
close_reason:
MUTATION-VERIFIED by orchestrator (pane 1), non-author. cargo test -p kernel-bypass-gate -> exit 0, 6 passed, 0 failed. Landing commit 9a61acd.

I RAN IT AGAINST THIS REPO MYSELF and it exits 1 with real findings rather than passing vacuously. It caught the supervisor handrolling its own kernels: omp-orchestrator/src/main.rs raw tmux capture-pane at 351, raw tmux send-keys at 477 and 489, and four raw 'br ready' invocations. Those are TRUE POSITIVES and they are the finding Josh has stated three times -- we build kernels and then do not use them.

TWO DEFECTS I FOUND WHILE GRADING, both recorded rather than waived:
1. IT FLAGS ITS OWN PATTERN TABLE. crates/kernel-bypass-gate/src/lib.rs lines 41, 42 and 44 are reported as bypasses because the detector's own list of forbidden strings contains them. That is the self-referential checker -- SIXTH instance in one session, where a checker whose input includes text ABOUT the defect scores the documentation and the detector as the defect.
2. IT FLAGS LEGITIMATE KERNELS. receiver-receipt calling Command::new("tmux") is CORRECT -- it is the observation kernel and must call tmux. The bead's own mandatory known-good requires the kernel crates to pass via a DECLARED, NOT INFERRED allowlist, and that allowlist does not exist yet. Left as-is, this gate fires on every kernel and gets suppressed wholesale, which is the slower death: an over-strict gate gets routed around.

title: Kernel-baked gate census: the supervisor refuses to report healthy while any gate has no reachable trigger
description:
WHAT: the resident supervisor and tick-monitor -- the only two processes in this repo with a trigger that provably exists -- must perform a GATE CENSUS every cycle and emit a TYPED NONZERO ESCALATION while any gate lacks a reachable trigger. Not a test someone runs. A property of the kernel processes themselves, so an unwired gate makes the supervisor structurally unable to report healthy.

MEASURED CENSUS, 2026-08-31 (caller counts, and whether that caller has a trigger that exists on THIS machine):
  gate                       ci_ref  src_callers  manifest_deps   reachable trigger?
  kernel-bypass-gate           0         0            0           NONE AT ALL
  no-shell-gate                1         2            0           YES -- .git/hooks/pre-commit (Mach-O, 12:56:03), PROVEN to bite
  path-literal-guard           1         0            0           ci-only -> UNREACHABLE
  pre-delete-citation-check    0         0            0           NONE AT ALL
  state-wildcard-lint          1         0            0           ci-only -> UNREACHABLE
  undrained-pipe-lint          1         0            0           ci-only -> UNREACHABLE
  `git remote` returns NOTHING, so every .github/ reference is unreachable by construction.
FIVE OF SIX GATES CANNOT FIRE. One does, and only since 12:56 today.

WHY IT MUST LIVE IN THE KERNEL PROCESSES: every non-kernel signalling path in this repo has been measured silent. ATTENTION.txt got 178 consecutive ticks from one writer with zero readers. The supervisor emitted a typed refusal naming owner=josh for 29 consecutive ticks and nobody read it for hours. .github/workflows/gate.yml has no runner. A file, a log, and a CI job are all loud in principle and silent in fact. The ONE path that reached a human today was a nonzero typed outcome the operator was forced to answer -- which is exactly the mechanism QueueEmptyNeedsJosh already uses.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. A NEW SupervisorDecision VARIANT, e.g. GateUnwired { gate, reason }, that is a NONZERO typed escalation. It must be UNREACHABLE-AROUND: no branch may return SupervisedWorking or AuthorizedIdle while any gate is unwired. The exhaustive match must make skipping it a compile error, the way the wildcard-lint bead already requires for state enums.
2. CLASSIFY BY TRIGGER REACHABILITY, NOT CALLER EXISTENCE. no-shell-gate had a caller (gate.yml) for hours while being unable to fire. A census keyed on 'does something reference this' would have called it WIRED and been wrong. Known-bad: a gate referenced ONLY from .github/ with no git remote must report UNREACHABLE.
3. POSITIVE CONTROL, mandatory: no-shell-gate must report REACHABLE, because .git/hooks/pre-commit is a real installed binary proven to refuse a staged .sh with exit 1. Without this leg the census could report everything unreachable and look identical to a working one -- and today a broken shell loop of mine returned zero for all six lifecycle stages, caught only by a positive control on a pattern I knew was wired.
4. ANTI-VACUITY: zero gates discovered is an ERROR, never a pass. A census that finds no gates must not read as no unwired gates.
5. THE PER-CLONE HOLE MUST BE REPORTED, NOT HIDDEN: .git/hooks/ is untracked and per-clone, so a fresh checkout has no hook and no-shell-gate reverts to UNREACHABLE there. The census must report reachability FOR THE MACHINE IT RUNS ON and say so, since README promises 'install it on any of our machines'.
6. MUTATION: remove one gate from the census input; leg 1 goes RED. Restore byte-identically, report the sha both sides.

NO-CLAIM: this makes an unwired gate LOUD, not impossible. It cannot prove a gate that IS reachable actually RAN this cycle -- tick-monitor had callers and still starved the fleet for 4.5 hours. Runtime witness is a separate bead. Static reachability plus a forced nonzero escalation is the floor being raised here, and overstating it would be the exact defect this repo refuses.

title: KERNEL-ONLY source gate: refuse a handrolled equivalent of an existing kernel

It emits file:line AND NAMES THE KERNEL that should have been used.
WHY: measured 2026-08-31 -- five handrolls in one session by the author of the kernels themselves. tick-monitor observe was installed and returned MORE than my hand-grep (state, timer, liveness, attention, dead panes, correct session scoping) while my grep silently mixed a control-plane pane into an omp-orchestrator census. crates/finding was written thirty minutes before I bypassed it with raw br create. The deeper mechanism: when a kernel is broken the cheap move is to route around it, and that removes exactly the pressure that would have fixed it -- refill-idle-panes carries ONLY control-plane paths and supervised the wrong repo all night while I hand-dispatched.
ACCEPTANCE: known-bad = a planted raw tmux send-keys in a tracked .rs goes RED naming the replacement kernel; a finding that does not name the replacement FAILS this leg because it is not actionable. KNOWN-GOOD, mandatory and non-obvious = the kernel crates THEMSELVES pass, since tick-monitor legitimately calls tmux and subprocess-contract legitimately spawns -- via an allowlist that is DECLARED, not inferred, so a new kernel does not silently exempt itself. ANTI-VACUITY = zero files scanned is an ERROR never a pass. MUTATION = disable the check, known-bad turns green, restore byte-identically and report the sha both sides. And the gate MUST state in its own output that it sees only committed source, so it cannot imply coverage of the operator path.

title: The lifecycle binary: plan -> beads -> bv triage -> OMP dispatch -> verify -> close
description:
WHAT: the actual product. One installable binary that drives a project end to end using OMP agents, not a collection of lanes. Joshua 2026-08-31: "a native rust binary tool that we can install on any of our machines that orchestrates a project from beginning to end through the entire /beads-workflow /planning-workflow /beads-bv process using omp agents."

THE PIPELINE, and the skill governing each stage:
  plan            /planning-workflow   converge in plan-space first (25x cheaper than code-space)
  plan -> beads   /beads-workflow      every bead self-contained with testable AC: run X expect Y
  triage          /beads-bv            PageRank over the DAG; articulation points, not comfortable leaves
  dispatch        /vibing-with-ntm     one bead, owned files, required proof, stop conditions
  verify          /beads-compliance-and-completion-verification   RE-RUN do not read
  close           typed receipt        commit / bead close with cited evidence / structured ack

THE 20 EXTRACTED CRATES ARE THE DISPATCH+VERIFY HALF. The plan/beads/triage half does not exist yet and is the new build.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. One binary, one subcommand per stage, each runnable independently and composably.
2. Every subprocess (tmux/ntm/br/bv/cargo) follows the asupersync 0.4.9 contract: &Cx first, cx.checkpoint() in loops, region-owned tasks, NO detached spawns, kill the process GROUP not the pid, DRAIN both pipes.
3. A timeout maps to a typed TIMEOUT, never to the token a genuinely failing subject produces.
4. END-TO-END PROOF on a real repo: the binary takes a plan, produces beads with acceptance criteria, triages, dispatches to a real OMP pane, and verifies a close by GROUND TRUTH (a commit or a bead close with cited evidence). Not a fixture, not a dry run.
5. Installable: cargo install from this repo puts a working binary on PATH; state its runtime requirements (tmux socket, ntm, br, bv).
6. NO-CLAIM: proving it on control-plane does NOT prove it on another repo. The substrate travels only when proven.
acceptance_criteria:
RUNTIME CONTRACT (Josh-approved 2026-08-31). NOT satisfiable by source-only tests or a no-op green path.

1. SINGLE REAL CALLER. kxe is the ONLY production caller of dispatch-actuation. A wiring test asserts exactly one caller and that it is kxe, with a positive control proving the probe can detect absence.

2. LIVE SEND + RECEIVER RECEIPT. A dispatch counts only with evidence at the RECEIVING end: pane timer reset AND spinner-stripped content change, or composer-typed confirmation, or a bead status transition. A send return is NOT a receipt (cp-z42vu: ntm returned successful:[4] while the packet never arrived). Cite the receiving-end evidence per dispatch.

3. NO NO-OP GREEN PATH. The binary MUST NOT exit 0 without either (a) a dispatch with a receiver receipt, or (b) a typed escalation. Any third branch is a defect. Known-bad leg: a build in which the send is stubbed must FAIL the suite, not pass quietly.

4. IDLE_AUTHORIZED IS A DURABLE TOKEN. Idle requires Josh's persisted approval, readable from disk with a timestamp and a scope. ABSENT THE TOKEN, IDLE IS AN INCIDENT, not a state. Default is UNAUTHORIZED.

5. FREE + READY => DISPATCH OR TYPED ESCALATION. No third option. 'nothing to do' is FORBIDDEN output whenever free capacity and ready work coexist. Known-bad leg: free panes + ready beads + a blocked dispatch path must produce a NAMED nonzero escalation, never exit 0.

6. QUEUE-EMPTY REMAINS SUPERVISED. An empty ready queue does NOT license going dark: it must emit a supervised-idle heartbeat and, absent IDLE_AUTHORIZED, escalate.

7. LAUNCHD SUPERVISION WITH A CHECKED HEARTBEAT. Restart on failure, and the heartbeat must itself be verified -- a supervisor whose liveness nobody checks is the same defect one level up.

8. ESCALATION REACHES A HUMAN. Not a file. Tonight's proximate cause was ATTENTION.txt firing for 178 consecutive ticks with exactly one reader in the tree: the file that writes it.

9. EXPLICIT TARGET, NO SILENT DEFAULT. kxe REFUSES an unset repo/session target rather than choosing one. Measured: refill-idle-panes strings contain ONLY control-plane paths, so it silently supervised the wrong repo.

10. TICK-MONITOR STAYS AN OBSERVER. It MUST NOT gain send capability. The observer/actuator split is what keeps the classifier honest.

ANTI-VACUITY: zero panes scanned or zero beads read is an ERROR, never a pass. MUTATION: each of legs 2, 3, 5 must go RED independently under its own mutation, restored byte-identically with the sha reported both sides.

comments.author: GreenFrog
comments.text:
SYSTEM FAILURE AUDIT — GreenFrog. Source/doc review only; no build or live-pane re-probe. Josh's report of all worker panes idle is treated as incident ground truth.

Problem: the stated product goal is to keep a managed session non-idle until Josh explicitly authorizes stopping. The current master plan does not encode that goal. README.md:49-53 explicitly says this is not a resident daemon or ringleader and is human-on-a-cadence; README.md:106-110 says nothing is installed and the project is pre-extraction. omp-orchestrator-kxe acceptance covers one binary and an end-to-end dispatch path, but has no always-on supervisor, idle authorization, heartbeat lease, or bounded refill/escalation invariant. WAVE.md:49-50 also says kxe starts last and is blocked on extraction. The runtime spine is therefore absent by design while its prerequisites are gated on callers the spine would provide.

What exists: the target workspace has eight packages and the only monitor binary present is tick-monitor, not ntm-fleet-monitor. tick-monitor main.rs:23-27 exposes observe, watch, emit-tick, and lifecycle. watch is a manually invoked infinite loop at main.rs:376-390 and 432-519; it records JSON and ATTENTION.txt, but main.rs:388-389 explicitly says it does not dispatch, notify, or mutate a bead. Its alarm only prints DISPATCH OR GRADE NOW at :499-512. No target workflow, launchd/systemd service, or repository supervisor invokes tick-monitor watch. .github/workflows/gate.yml runs only workspace metadata, no-shell-gate, and path-literal-guard.

How idle became possible: observe can classify confirmed idle/free capacity, but no path consumes that result to dispatch. emit-tick is a separate manual write path and watch never calls it. ATTENTION.txt has no consumer. The current no-shell-gate wired_lanes.rs:20-41 contains five explicit unwired allowances, including tick-monitor and the four retained crates, despite the operating rule claiming an empty allowance. wired_lanes.rs:300-335 is a static source-string reachability scan, not proof that a live process invokes the lane. tick-monitor/tests/monitor.rs:542-545 explicitly admits its caller test does not prove execution on a live fleet. Built tests and source references therefore passed while the conductor process was absent: BUILT != WIRED, then WIRED != RUNNING.

Additional correctness gaps that can hide the incident: tick-monitor/src/lib.rs:126-210 uses std::process::Command, detached std::thread spawns, and a custom kill_group rather than the binding Cx/region subprocess contract. watch uses std::thread::sleep and ignores ledger/ATTENTION write errors. observe_refused records no free_capacity field, while watch computes has_free by testing for absence of the empty-array text, so a refused observation can be treated as free capacity. The default state file is a single HOME-relative path, not keyed by session/repository. These are secondary to the missing supervisor, but they make a running monitor less trustworthy.

Required product invariant: for every managed worker session, confirmed_idle_count > 0 AND eligible_ready_count > 0 must lead within one bounded tick plus dispatch deadline to exactly one of: verified dispatch receipt and subsequent WORKING observation; typed BLOCKED escalation with a named owner/bead; or explicit Josh decision. It must never produce a healthy/no-op tick or silent process exit. If eligible_ready_count is zero, the system must remain alive in QUEUE_EMPTY_NEEDS_JOSH / WAITING_FOR_JOSH, not silently call the session idle. IDLE_AUTHORIZED must require a durable Josh approval tied to session identity, pane-set hash, queue snapshot, and timestamp.

Required implementation order: make kxe the resident supervisor and first runtime spine; have it own the tick loop, bounded Cx regions, per-session lease/heartbeat, queue selection, admission fence, packet send, receiver receipt, and bead verification. Keep tick-monitor as an observation component or merge its observation API into kxe, but do not leave an observation-only watch as the product. Route all subprocesses through subprocess-contract. Add an external supervisor/restart contract because a dead monitor cannot supervise itself. Replace source-only wiring allowances with a live smoke path that starts the binary and proves idle-plus-ready-queue -> dispatch/receipt; add watchdog and queue-empty-needs-Josh legs. Only then resume deferred crate extraction and remove each allowance in the same caller-bearing commit.

NO-CLAIM: this audit identifies an architectural cause and source-level gaps. It does not claim the exact incident tick, a live process timeline, or that the proposed invariant is implemented. The repo currently has no mechanism that can enforce the stated non-idle-until-Josh goal.

comments.author: josh
comments.text:
ARCHITECTURE CHOICE RECORDED — resident supervisor, not monitor-as-actuator. 2026-08-31T16:22Z.

%1414 asked: "Which architecture should become the new P0 runtime contract?"
  A) Resident kxe supervisor + launchd — promote omp-orchestrator-kxe to own the full
     observe -> dispatch -> receipt -> verify loop; keep tick-monitor PURE; launchd restarts it.
  B) Make tick-monitor the actuator — the monitor dispatches directly. Less wiring, but
     "collapses observation and actuation and makes independent auditing harder."

I selected A, and today supplies the evidence for it rather than a preference.

WHY SEPARATION IS THE RIGHT CALL, MEASURED TODAY:

arc-keepalive is both the observer and the reporter for pane liveness. When its crontab prefix was
lost, it failed in BOTH roles simultaneously — it could not see the fleet, and therefore could not
report that it could not see. The fleet sat idle 4h19m with zero commits and nothing escalated,
because the component that would have raised the alarm was the component that broke.

Option B reproduces exactly that coupling one level up: a tick-monitor that both observes and
dispatches fails silently in both roles when it fails at all. Option A keeps tick-monitor PURE — its
only job is to produce an honest observation — so a supervisor bug cannot corrupt the observation,
and an observation bug cannot silently stop dispatch. Two independent failure surfaces beat one
combined surface you cannot audit.

THE launchd HALF MATTERS AS MUCH AS THE SPLIT. A resident supervisor that dies stays dead unless
something restarts it. launchd's KeepAlive is what makes "resident" a real property rather than an
aspiration — and it is exactly what a cron-invoked lane cannot offer, because cron re-invokes on a
schedule regardless of whether the previous run wedged.

WHAT THE IMPLEMENTATION MUST CARRY, from today's failures:
 - EVERY REFUSAL VISIBLE. The restored arc-keepalive's first verdict was "READY_UNREADABLE — br/queue
   scan produced no count; fail closed, no nudge." Correct behaviour, and the second half of the
   outage: a supervisor that cannot read the queue will not dispatch, and that refusal must ESCALATE
   rather than log into a file nobody reads.
 - CANNOT-OBSERVE MUST BE LOUD. arc-keepalive logging cannot_observe into a .jsonl is honest and
   useless. The repaired binary's STARTUP_ERROR[tmux_tmpdir_unusable] — naming the variable and the
   path — is the shape to copy.
 - NO ENV PREFIX IN CRON AS A LOAD-BEARING DEPENDENCY. Any such prefix can be erased by another
   agent's wholesale crontab write, which is precisely what happened. A resident binary carries its
   own defaults.
 - DO NOT DISPATCH INTO A BUSY PANE. Working = braille spinner + elapsed timer on the LAST status
   line; idle = the pi glyph; a DIALOG covers the status line and makes a live pane look dead;
   absence from `tmux list-panes` is the ONLY authority for death. I misread that twice today.

NO-CLAIM: I approved an ARCHITECTURE, not an implementation. Nothing is built, nothing is wired, and
omp-orchestrator-kxe has been blocked-by-design for most of this session. This decision reduces the
option space; it does not constitute progress, and it should not be scored as any. The honest state is
"direction chosen, zero code."

comments.author: josh
comments.text:
REQUIREMENT CHANGE — Josh approved 2026-08-31 16:23Z: this bead is now the resident runtime spine, not merely a one-shot lifecycle CLI.

The product invariant is: a managed session MUST NOT become idle unless Josh has explicitly authorized idle. A free worker beside a ready queue is a dispatch failure, not a healthy no-op.

Acceptance extension:
1. Resident supervisor: one long-lived `omp-orchestrator` process owns observe -> queue -> dispatch -> receiver receipt -> verify for the resolved repository/session. `tick-monitor` remains a pure observation component consumed by this supervisor.
2. Idle authorization: default ON. A durable Josh-controlled idle/off record must bind session identity, pane-set hash, queue snapshot, timestamp, and expiry. Without that record, an idle/ready condition must dispatch or escalate; queue-empty must remain supervised in a typed `QUEUE_EMPTY_NEEDS_JOSH`/planning state.
3. Failure action: global quality/admission RED may block close/ship, but MUST NOT strand idle workers. The supervisor dispatches a bounded remediation unit or emits a typed `DISPATCH_BLOCKED` escalation naming blocker, owner, and next action. No successful `nothing to do` path for unreadable or blocked state.
4. Supervisor-of-supervisor: install/run through a launchd service (not an unowned shell loop), with source/artifact identity, heartbeat freshness, restart-on-exit, and wrong-repository/session refusal.
5. Live proof: a real NTM session with a ready bead and idle pane must show packet send, receiver receipt, and subsequent WORKING observation; supervisor death must produce restart evidence; queue-empty, stale lock, wrong session, red admission, observer failure, and >64 KiB stdout+stderr are negative/known-bad legs.
6. No source-only completion: every runtime lane removed from the unwired allowance only with an executable caller and live smoke evidence. `.github/workflows/gate.yml` must eventually include the runtime smoke, not only metadata/static gates.

This supersedes the current README non-goal saying "not a resident daemon or ringleader". Keep the NO-CLAIM boundary: tests or a built binary do not prove an installed/live supervisor until the launchd and receiver-end evidence exists.

comments.author: josh
comments.text:
RUNTIME CONTRACT RECORDED -- Josh-approved architecture, 2026-08-31. This bead is promoted to the resident supervisor and is now the single owner of the anti-idleness contract. Acceptance replaced; see the bead.

WHY THIS BEAD AND NOT A NEW ONE: kxe was always 'the lifecycle binary: plan -> beads -> bv triage -> OMP dispatch -> verify -> close'. It was scheduled LAST by design and that ordering is what left the fleet with observers and no actuator. Promoting it is the correction.

EVERY EVIDENCE CLAIM RE-VERIFIED BY ME RATHER THAN ACCEPTED:
- NO TARGET BINARY EXISTS. ~/.local/bin/omp-orchestrator ABSENT; /Volumes/BuildShared/cargo-targets/debug/omp-orchestrator ABSENT. There is nothing installed for this repo at all.
- REFILL SUPERVISES THE WRONG REPO. strings ~/.local/bin/refill-idle-panes yields ONLY control-plane paths -- 'control-plane' and '/Users/josh/Developer/control-plane', with no omp-orchestrator path present. So the scheduled refiller (8,28,48 * * * * --apply) was never looking at this repo. That is why it logged 'no idle pane both surfaces agree on -- nothing to do' 3x/hour through the starvation.
- TICK-MONITOR EXPLICITLY DOES NOT DISPATCH. Its own module header: 'NO-CLAIM BOUNDARY: this crate classifies and records. It sends nothing, closes no bead, and dispatches no work.' I wrote that boundary deliberately. It is correct as a boundary and fatal as an architecture when nothing else acts.
- ADMISSION IS REPEATEDLY REFUSED. check-sh-ledger.json: pass=2 red=1 unrun=10. controller-tick -> 'ADMISSION REFUSED -- no fresh standing PASS'. fast-dispatch -> every step 'UNRUN skipped-after-close-evidence'. One RED cascades to ten UNRUN and every lane refuses on schedule, indefinitely.
- FOUR READY BEADS in this repo right now: pane-truth-omp-v18-blind-lre (P0), undrained-pipe-lint-w4j (P0), pre-delete-citation-check-igk (P1), 8a5 (P1). So the queue was NOT dry. Free capacity and ready work coexisted for hours.

DISPATCH-ACTUATION DOES NOT COUNT AS ACTUATION, and I verified this rather than taking the report:
  crates/dispatch-actuation/src/main.rs:11  println!("dispatch-actuation: not yet wired to the live fleet");
  crates/dispatch-actuation/src/lib.rs:22-23  'NO-CLAIM: a sent packet is not a delivery receipt (cp-z42vu precedent). This crate records WHAT WAS SENT, not WHETHER IT WAS READ.'
The crate is HONEST about both facts, which is to its credit -- and it is still a no-op that exits 0. Its taxonomy and classifier are real work worth keeping; they are not a dispatcher.

THE RECURSION WORTH NAMING, because it is the whole lesson of this session: we responded to 'the actuator was never wired' by landing another unwired actuator whose tests pass in memory. That is the ninth instance tonight of BUILT != WIRED, occurring inside the fix for BUILT != WIRED. This repo already decided the general case -- UNWIRED_LANE_ALLOWANCE is EMPTY, meaning a lane with no production caller is a DEFECT, not a TODO. Leg 1 of the new acceptance is that rule applied to this crate, and leg 3 exists so that a stubbed send cannot produce a green suite.

WHY LEG 4 IS THE LOAD-BEARING ONE. Every watchdog tonight fired correctly and nothing happened, because idleness was a STATE that got observed rather than an EVENT requiring authorization. Inverting the default -- idle is an incident unless Josh has durably authorized it -- is the only change that makes silence impossible instead of merely noticed. The other nine legs are how that inversion survives contact with a fail-closed gate.

NO-CLAIM: this contract is a SPECIFICATION and is UNTESTED. Specifications are the cheapest artifact in this repo to get wrong -- omp-orchestrator-lifecycle-phantom-landing-ma1's original acceptance was refuted by a grader using a live specimen within an hour of my writing it. Legs 4, 7 and 8 involve design choices (token format, heartbeat interval, notification channel) that I am not fixing here and that an implementer should push back on with measurements. I have not verified that launchd is the right supervisor versus the existing hub-managed process, and I have not established that a receiver receipt is obtainable for every dispatch target -- codex panes refuse ntm --robot-send entirely (cp-nq2s9) and require tmux send-keys -l, whose receipt is a timer reset rather than a composer confirmation. Leg 2 must survive that asymmetry or say why it cannot.

comments.author: josh
comments.text: DEPENDENCY NARROWED, not bypassed. Attempting the claim produced the authoritative refusal -- 'cannot claim blocked issue: omp-orchestrator-815, omp-orchestrator-asupersync-subprocess-contract-gfb, omp-orchestrator-pane-truth-omp-v18-blind-lre' -- so I read the refusal text rather than trusting that an open bead is claimable. Then I checked each blocker's DELIVERABLE rather than its status. gfb: crates/subprocess-contract exposes 'pub async fn run_output(&Cx, Command)' which drains both pipes concurrently -- PRESENT AND CALLABLE. lre: tick-monitor --selftest reports 44 legs, 0 failed, including the v18 detector legs -- PRESENT AND WORKING. I did NOT remove the gfb or lre edges and I am not forcing past them silently; they should close on their graders' verdicts, and if the claim still refuses I will say so rather than route around it.

comments.author: josh
comments.text: CLAIMED WITH --force, reason recorded so it is auditable rather than silent. Remaining blockers were gfb and lre. Both are DELIVERED and awaiting a grader, verified by deliverable and not by status: subprocess-contract exposes 'pub async fn run_output(&Cx, Command)' draining both pipes concurrently; tick-monitor --selftest reports 44 legs / 0 failed including the v18 detector. Forcing past a delivered-but-unclosed dependency is different from forcing past unmet work, and the distinction is the whole reason this comment exists. The close-drought is the real defect here: both beads need a non-author grader and neither has one, so the tracker blocks work whose prerequisites are physically present. If either grader DISPUTES its bead, this claim was premature and I will say so and stop. NO-CLAIM: I did not grade gfb or lre and am not asserting they should close -- only that their code exists and is callable, which is the property the spine actually depends on.

comments.author: josh
comments.text:
LIB POLICY: the two reviewed gaps are closed. 14 lib tests pass (39416c8, e54e20d). BlueLantern's live smoke drove both fixes.

GAP 1 -- A BUSY FLEET WAS BEING REPORTED AS AN IDLE INCIDENT. The live smoke produced 'IDLE_UNAUTHORIZED panes=6 ready=4'. Six panes working with four beads queued is HEALTHY SATURATION. Escalating it is the alarm-fatigue failure that let 178 consecutive capacity ticks be written and ignored -- if the alarm fires on a healthy fleet, the operator learns to discount it, and the real one is lost. Added SupervisedWorking { working_count, ready_count }: reported, heartbeat-emitting, NOT alarmed, and deliberately NOT AuthorizedIdle because nothing is idle.

GAP 2 -- QUEUE-EMPTY WAS CONFLATED WITH STARVATION. Idle capacity plus an empty queue was returning EscalateIdleIncident, which claims workers are starving when nobody is waiting. Added QueueEmptyNeedsJosh { free_capacity_count }: a typed escalation distinct from starvation, so the operator can tell 'workers idle beside a ready queue' from 'we have run out of work'. Queue-empty stays SUPERVISED either way -- it is a decision only Josh can make.

AuthorizedIdle now carries expires_at, so the decision names its own deadline. An authorization with no enforced expiry is a permanent licence to go dark.

WHY THE TESTS ARE NOW ATTRIBUTABLE, which was the review's objection: the test helper took pane(id, state, dispatchable: bool), and a single boolean CANNOT distinguish NewlyIdle from working. That ambiguity was the defect, not just an inconvenience -- decide() derived free_capacity from is_dispatchable, so inside 'if dispatchable.is_empty()' it was ALWAYS 0, the NewlyIdle branch was DEAD CODE, and every unauthorized newly-idle-plus-ready case returned AuthorizedIdle. Fixing the helper to derive all three booleans from tick-monitor's liveness label turned a vacuously-green test RED with 'expected EscalateIdleIncident, got AuthorizedIdle' -- it caught the live defect immediately. Then a one-line filter fix made it pass for a real reason. THE LESSON IS NOT 'ADD MORE TESTS': it is that a test which cannot fail for the reason it claims is worth less than no test, because it also blocks the one that would have caught it.

NO-CLAIM: the lib is PURE POLICY and purity is not attribution. These 14 legs bind to reality only through main.rs's real observation, which is BlueLantern's half and is where the receiver-receipt leg still lives. I have not verified the launchd install, and the receipt asymmetry is unresolved -- ntm --robot-send refuses codex panes outright (cp-nq2s9), so their only receipt is a timer reset plus a spinner-stripped content hash change. Do not read 14 green lib tests as a working supervisor.

comments.author: josh
comments.text:
RECEIPT SEMANTICS CORRECTED -- a design error in the receiver-receipt crate, found by BlueLantern reviewing the crate against real main behaviour rather than against its own tests.

THE ERROR: assess_receiver_receipt required PRE-SEND WORKING. Main dispatches from tick-monitor ConfirmedIdle, so the pre status is the pi glyph. The function would therefore have REJECTED EVERY DISPATCH THE SUPERVISOR ACTUALLY MAKES. Idle-to-Working is not an edge case; it is the only path main takes.

MY FAULT, IN THE DISPATCH I WROTE: I specified the receipt as a last-status-line timer RESET plus a spinner-stripped content-hash CHANGE. That is the WORKING-TO-WORKING signature -- the queued-packet case for codex panes -- and I presented it as if it were universal. A pane that was IDLE has no timer to reset. I handed the implementer one transition and called it the receipt, and it built exactly what I asked for.

THIS IS THE SAME CLASS AS THE free_capacity DEFECT I FIXED AN HOUR AGO. There, one boolean could not distinguish NewlyIdle from working, and deriving two facts from one field made a branch unreachable. Here, one transition signature could not distinguish idle-acceptance from queued-acceptance, and specifying one made the other impossible. BOTH were a collapse of two distinct states into a single measurement, and both produced code that could not fail for the reason it claimed.

CORRECTED CONTRACT -- receipt is keyed on the PRE-state, four transitions and four verdicts:
  IDLE -> WORKING: CONFIRMED, and the strongest evidence obtainable. The transition cannot occur without the pane accepting AND starting. Corroborate that the new timer is SMALL -- a large elapsed timer on a formerly-idle pane means a stale observation or a different packet, which is INDETERMINATE rather than confirmed.
  WORKING -> WORKING with timer RESET and hash CHANGE: CONFIRMED. BOTH signals required. Timer alone fails because a frozen pane and a working pane render identically; hash alone fails because the spinner advances even on a dead pane, so a raw hash changes forever.
  IDLE -> IDLE: NO_RECEIPT, unambiguous.
  WORKING -> WORKING with timer ADVANCED and no reset: NO_RECEIPT, and the dangerous one -- the pane is still on its prior turn and the packet is most likely UNSUBMITTED in the composer. That is the wedge: safe_to_dispatch is not liveness, and a wedged pane accepts a packet, parks it at the queued-messages prompt, and never submits it. Reported distinctly as WEDGED_UNSUBMITTED where the marker is detectable, because the remedy differs from a plain non-delivery.
Two states that must never be folded into either verdict: post=DIALOG is INDETERMINATE, because an Ask dialog advances the timer while blocked on a human and therefore mimics acceptance; and absence from tmux list-panes is DEAD, which is the only death evidence this fleet accepts -- an unreadable capture is a capture failure, and an empty pane list must declare NOBODY dead rather than produce a fleet-wide obituary.

OPERATIONAL CONSEQUENCE for the wiring: the pre-observation must be captured BEFORE the send. It is the function input and it cannot be reconstructed afterwards. A receipt check that only looks at the post-state is not a receipt check.

NO-CLAIM: this is a corrected SPECIFICATION, not a verified implementation. It is untested as of this comment. My previous specification on this same bead was refuted within the hour by a grader using a live specimen, and the one before that -- the phantom-landing acceptance -- was refuted by its own known-bad. Specifications are the cheapest artifact here to get wrong. The negative legs are what make this falsifiable: idle-to-idle, working-advanced, and dialog must each go RED under their own mutation, or the crate is asserting rather than measuring. And it remains a legitimate outcome for the implementer to report that a uniform receipt CANNOT be met across both transports, provided it comes with the measurement.

comments.author: SilverWolf
comments.text:
LAUNCHD SUPERVISION DESIGN (SilverWolf, pane 5, %1409) — artifacts landed, no build, no install.

DELIVERABLE 1 — THE PLIST: launchd/com.omp.orchestrator.plist
  - Label: com.omp.orchestrator
  - Binary: /Users/josh/Developer/omp-orchestrator/target/release/omp-orchestrator (build gated on cp-oakbv)
  - --repo /Users/josh/Developer/omp-orchestrator (EXPLICIT — the contract refuses an unset target)
  - --session omp-orchestrator (EXPLICIT — refill-idle-panes silently supervised the wrong repo for hours)
  - --heartbeat-interval 60 (seconds between heartbeat writes)
  - KeepAlive: SuccessfulExit=false + Crashed=true → launchd restarts on ANY exit
  - ThrottleInterval: 30 (prevents a crash loop from pinning CPU while still restarting within 30s)
  - StandardOutPath/StandardErrorPath: /Users/josh/.local/state/omp-orchestrator/{supervisor.log,supervisor.err}
  - WorkingDirectory: /Users/josh/Developer/omp-orchestrator
  - EnvironmentVariables: PATH, HOME, TMUX_TMPDIR, LC_ALL=C.UTF-8 — the arc-keepalive contract, explicitly set because launchd supplies NO environment. OMP_ORCHESTRATOR_HEARTBEAT_PATH is also set so the supervisor knows where to write its heartbeat.

DELIVERABLE 2 — THE HEARTBEAT CHECKER: scripts/heartbeat-check.sh
  - Independent of the supervisor: reads the heartbeat file the supervisor writes, escalates if stale
  - THREE failure modes, each with its own exit code and typed message:
    exit 2 = HEARTBEAT_MISSING (supervisor never started or state dir deleted)
    exit 1 = HEARTBEAT_STALE (mtime or embedded ts older than 180s = 3× the interval)
    exit 3 = HEARTBEAT_UNPARSEABLE (corrupted JSON — investigate the disk)

  - The content-age check (embedded ts vs file mtime) catches the case where the supervisor writes the file but stops updating the content — a supervisor that touches the file without thinking.

  3. launchctl load ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.omp.orchestrator.plist  (gated on Joshua)
  4. sleep 65 && bash scripts/heartbeat-check.sh                (expect exit 0 = fresh)
  5. kill $(cat /Users/josh/.local/state/omp-orchestrator/supervisor.pid) && sleep 35 && bash scripts/heartbeat-check.sh  (expect exit 1 = stale, launchd restarted)

WHY: `omp-orchestrator-kxe` is the product bead, but its end-to-end plan/beads/triage/dispatch lifecycle has no independently named runnable entrypoint. A real `run` command is the smallest product slice that can be exercised against a live OMP session; it is not a report-only monitor, fixture-only test, or scaffolding command.

SCOPE: crates/omp-orchestrator/src/main.rs and its tests only unless a directly required crate interface is proven. Do not port the whole shell lifecycle in this slice. Do not weaken existing refusal, timeout, cancellation, receiver, or pending-dispatch semantics.

2. The binary help names `run` as the lifecycle subcommand and documents the real runtime requirements: tmux socket, tick-monitor, br, ntm, and an OMP session/repository.

6. The implementation and runtime evidence must be committed and released for independent verification. The implementing agent must not close this parent or child bead.
