title: tick-monitor lifecycle attributes CITED SHAs as a bead's own landing, inflating LANDED_UNGRADED with phantom work
description:
WHAT: `tick-monitor lifecycle` harvests commit SHAs from a bead's PROSE and records them as that bead's own landing. A SHA cited as ANOTHER bead's evidence therefore promotes the citing bead into LANDED_UNGRADED, so the grading queue fills with beads where nothing was ever built.

MEASURED 2026-08-31, found by a grader disputing my premise rather than by me:
  tick-monitor lifecycle reported: omp-orchestrator-2lo  author=-  deps=0  landed=3f821d4
  git log --all --grep='2lo'      -> EMPTY. No commit references 2lo at all.
  git log -1 3f821d4              -> 'gate: no-shell-gate - fail the build on tracked .sh/.py [mutation-verified]'
                                    which is omp-orchestrator-4ak's work, not 2lo's.
  3f821d4 in 2lo's comments      -> present, as a CITATION, in a comment I wrote myself.
So the tool read my own cross-reference to a different bead's commit and reported it as this bead's implementation.

IMPACT, and it is a ROUTING-SAFETY defect rather than a cosmetic one. LANDED_UNGRADED is what I use to decide who grades what. A phantom row causes a grader to be dispatched at a bead with no artifact, which is a wasted slot under a build freeze when grading is the only work available. Worse, it is INDISTINGUISHABLE from real work in the output: the row carries a real SHA that resolves in git, so a conductor checking 'does the cited commit exist?' gets YES and proceeds. It took a grader re-deriving the premise -- `git log --grep` on the bead id -- to catch it. That check is exactly what the tool should be doing and is not.

THIRD DEFECT IN THIS TOOL IN ONE SESSION, and all three are the same failure of attribution:
  1. author= reads the current ASSIGNEE, not the implementer. Observed live: r3h flipped author=GreenFrog -> author=AmberGate when I routed AmberGate as its GRADER. I nearly handed a bead back to its own implementer.
  2. dangling SHA citations were counted as unresolvable commits -- fixed in fa5129e/b352af1 by requiring `in_citation_position` for marker words and excluding truncated sha256 content hashes.
  3. THIS: a SHA in citation position is still credited as a landing. Fix (2) narrowed which TOKENS count as commit-shaped; it never asked WHOSE commit a resolvable SHA is.
The generalisation the tool keeps failing: a SHA appearing NEAR a bead is not a SHA belonging to that bead. Adjacency is not authorship -- the same lesson as the DIALOG detector, where a framed marker in scrollback is not a dialog, and only ADJACENCY TO THE STATUS LINE discriminated.

THE FIX, stated as a contract rather than a patch:
A bead's landing set must be derived from the OBJECT STORE keyed on the bead, not from the bead's text. The authoritative join is `git log --all --grep=<bead-short-id>`: the commit must NAME the bead. A SHA that appears only in prose is a CITATION and belongs in a separate field -- `cites=` -- which must never feed LANDED_UNGRADED.
That also fixes defect 1 in the same pass: the implementer is the author of the commits in the derived landing set, and where the landing set is empty there IS no implementer, so `author=` must render as NONE rather than borrowing the assignee.

ACCEPTANCE - must FIRES-ON-KNOWN-BAD, and the known-bad already exists in the tracker:
1. PLANTED (real specimen, no fixture needed): run lifecycle over this repo. omp-orchestrator-2lo must NOT appear in LANDED_UNGRADED and must NOT carry landed=3f821d4. It is now CLOSED, so use a scratch bead citing a foreign SHA if a live open specimen is needed.
2. KNOWN-GOOD leg, mandatory: a bead WITH a real commit naming it (e.g. 4ak / 3f821d4, or npq / f9f4e37) must STILL appear with its landing intact. Without this leg the fix ships an over-strict rule that empties the queue and gets routed around.
3. author= must render NONE for a bead with an empty landing set, and must NOT equal the assignee. Assert on a bead whose assignee is set and whose landing set is empty -- 2lo before its close was exactly that shape.
4. cites= must be POPULATED for the citation case, so the information is preserved rather than deleted. A fix that silently drops the cross-reference loses the audit trail I was building when I wrote it.
5. MUTATION: revert to prose-harvesting -> leg 1 must go RED. Restore byte-identically and report the sha both sides.
6. ANTI-VACUITY: an empty bead set must be an ERROR, not a pass. A lifecycle run that parses zero beads currently reports 'zero beads parsed; an empty scan set is an ERROR, never a pass' -- keep that.

BLOCKED ON cp-oakbv: the fix requires `cargo build` and builds are refused fleet-wide (CARGO_MINT_CONTAINER_EXHAUSTED / cargo_floor_guard exit 75, refused even at CARGO_MINT_MIN_CONTAINER_PCT=7). I am not lowering the override further and not editing the installed default. Until the floor clears, LANDED_UNGRADED must be treated as an UPPER BOUND on real ungraded work, and every row confirmed with `git log --all --grep=<bead-id>` before a grader is dispatched at it.

NO-CLAIM: I have not audited how many CURRENT LANDED_UNGRADED rows are phantoms. 2lo is one confirmed instance; the count is unknown and I am not guessing it, because a remembered number dying on derivation is the exact failure class this session has produced four times. I also have not verified whether the `deps=` field suffers the same prose-harvesting problem, though `dep_count` was already found once to be measuring OUT-edges only.

comments.text:
NOT CLOSING, and the grade is the reason. SilverWolf's derivation (%1409) did not merely confirm this defect -- it REFUTED THE FIX I PROPOSED IN THIS BEAD'S OWN ACCEPTANCE, using a live specimen. A bead whose acceptance is disproven cannot close on the evidence that disproved it. Acceptance rewritten below; status stays blocked.

WHAT THE GRADER ESTABLISHED, with the denominator stated: 7 rows / 11 SHA claims. Controls PASSED -- 4ak and npq both REAL -- so the method discriminates and a spectacular all-phantom result was not what it produced. Results: REAL 1 (v18-blind, 8eed3b3 names the bead), REAL-WORK-UNNAMED 3 (5cl, 6gq, ma1 -- the work EXISTS, the citation contract failed), PHANTOM 5 (ma1 self-referential, r3h, he6, 815, 6gq).

I VERIFIED BOTH STRUCTURAL FINDINGS MYSELF RATHER THAN ACCEPTING THEM.

FINDING 1 -- CROSS-REPO SHA ELIGIBILITY, a fourth defect in this tool. CONFIRMED:
    (cd omp-orchestrator && git cat-file -e 8fc3e4b) -> does NOT have it
    (cd control-plane    && git cat-file -e 8fc3e4b) -> HAS IT: 'chore(safety): forbid unsafe in ported crates [test]'
So 8fc3e4b exists ONLY in control-plane, and my tool -- handed --repo for both -- resolved a control-plane commit as an omp-orchestrator bead's landing. The SHA resolves, so every 'does the cited commit exist?' check answers YES. Silent repo-membership failure, exactly as the grader named it. A bead belongs to ONE tracker; its landing set must be resolved in THAT repo, and a SHA resolvable only in a sibling repo is a cross-repo citation, not a landing.

FINDING 2 -- AND THIS IS THE ONE THAT KILLS MY PROPOSED CONTRACT. CONFIRMED, and worse than reported:
    git log -1 610569f            -> 'feat(extraction): add five crates (code-first, test pending)'   <- the REAL 815 work
    git log --all --grep='815'    -> e4a4b63 ONLY: 'chore(beads): consolidate orchestrator work into this tracker'
My proposed fix in the acceptance above was: 'the authoritative join is git log --all --grep=<bead-short-id>; the commit must NAME the bead.' Run on 815, that join returns e4a4b63 -- THE COMMIT THAT CREATED THE BEADS -- and MISSES 610569f, the commit that did the work. So the fix I specified would credit bead CREATION as bead IMPLEMENTATION while dropping the actual extraction. It is wrong in BOTH directions at once, on the very row the grader flagged.

The grader's formulation is exact and I am adopting it verbatim: MY OWN RULE -- 'mention is not implementation' -- APPLIES TO THE JOIN ITSELF. I narrowed the tool from harvesting mentions in bead prose to harvesting mentions in commit messages, and called the second one authoritative. Both are mention-based. I moved the defect across the join and declared it fixed.

WORSE, AND I AM RECORDING IT AGAINST MYSELF: I FOUND THIS EXACT REFUTATION HOURS AGO AND FAILED TO PROPAGATE IT. Earlier tonight, computing a grading backlog, I wrote that my probe 'matched e4a4b63 chore(beads): consolidate... for 5cl, he6 and 815 -- that is the tracker commit, not implementation, so backlog_count=4 is not trustworthy', and I switched to deriving from known commits instead. Then I wrote e4a4b63's exact failure mode into this bead as the authoritative fix. The measurement was already in this session's record; the doctrine did not reach the bead. That is the same shape as this repo's stale-context trap -- a correction that lives only in a transcript expires with the turn that produced it, and the only durable home is the artifact.

THE THIRD CATEGORY IS THE MOST VALUABLE THING IN THIS GRADE. REAL-WORK-UNNAMED (3 of 7) is a category my binary contract would have DESTROYED: it collapses PHANTOM and REAL-WORK-UNNAMED into one bucket, so a bead whose work genuinely landed but whose commit forgot to name it would be reported as 'nothing was built' -- and a conductor would then dispatch a grader at real, finished work as though it were vapour. That is a WORSE failure than the phantom rows I filed this bead about, because a phantom wastes a slot while a mislabelled real landing discards evidence.

ACCEPTANCE -- REPLACING THE ORIGINAL, which is withdrawn as refuted:
1. THREE-VALUED OUTPUT, never binary. REAL (a commit names the bead AND touches paths in the bead's scope), REAL-WORK-UNNAMED (paths in scope changed, no commit names the bead), PHANTOM (no work, SHA appears only in prose). Collapsing the middle value is the defect, not the fix.
2. REPO MEMBERSHIP is a precondition, not a lookup. Resolve every SHA in the repo that OWNS the bead. A SHA resolvable only in a sibling repo renders as cross_repo_citation and NEVER as a landing. Known-bad specimen: 8fc3e4b against an omp-orchestrator bead.
3. TRACKER COMMITS ARE NOT IMPLEMENTATIONS. A commit whose only changed paths are under .beads/ can never be a landing for any bead. Known-bad specimen: e4a4b63 must NOT be returned as 815's landing. This leg is what my withdrawn contract fails.
4. FALSE-NEGATIVE LEG, mandatory and previously absent: 610569f MUST be attributable to 815 by whatever join replaces the grep. A contract that only suppresses false positives while silently dropping real work has moved the error, not removed it.
5. KNOWN-GOOD control preserved: 4ak/3f821d4 and npq/f9f4e37 must remain REAL. The grader's controls passed and must keep passing.
6. field named `claims=` or `landing_evidence=`, NOT `landed=`. A message convention is a CLAIM about authorship. The field name must not assert more than the mechanism can establish -- that is this repo's own overclaim rule applied to a column header.
7. MUTATION on each of legs 2, 3, 4 independently, restored byte-identically with the sha reported both sides. Three defects were merged into one 'attribution' bug once already; each guard must fail on its own known-bad.
8. ANTI-VACUITY: zero beads parsed is an ERROR, never a pass (already present, keep it).

STATUS: stays BLOCKED on cp-oakbv. The fix needs cargo build and builds are refused fleet-wide (cargo_floor_guard exit 75, refused even at CARGO_MINT_MIN_CONTAINER_PCT=7). I am not lowering the override and not editing the installed default. The interim operating rule STRENGTHENS on this grade: LANDED_UNGRADED is an upper bound, AND a row that greps clean is not thereby phantom -- check whether the work landed under a commit that simply failed to name the bead, because 3 of 7 rows are that case.

NO-CLAIM: I did not re-derive the grader's 7-row / 11-SHA census; I verified its two structural findings and the two specimens that refute my contract. The rewritten acceptance is UNTESTED -- it is a specification, and specifications are the cheapest thing in this repo to get wrong, as this bead just demonstrated. Legs 1 and 6 are judgement calls about output shape and naming, not measurements, and a future grader should say so if it disagrees. I have not audited whether `deps=` suffers the same cross-repo membership failure, though `dep_count` was already found once to be measuring OUT-edges only.

title: MISSION: 100% OMP surface coverage in asupersync-native, cancel-correct crates
description:
THE MISSION, stated by Josh 2026-08-31: 100% coverage. Every single OMP surface lives in an asupersync-native, memory-safe, cancel-correct crate baked into our processes. The entire journey from idea to shipped product is typed, logged, observable, and reachable by a quick robot command.

THE DENOMINATOR, measured against the INSTALLED source (/Users/josh/.local/lib/node_modules/@oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent, v18.0.11, dist/cli.js 19M). Print these commands beside their output; do not inherit the numbers:
  find dist/types -maxdepth 1 -mindepth 1 -type d | wc -l        -> 57  type-surface directories
  find dist/types -maxdepth 1 -mindepth 1 -name '*.d.ts' | wc -l -> 14  top-level declaration files
  omp --help, COMMANDS block                                     -> 39  CLI subcommands
  --mode=<text|json|rpc|rpc-ui>                                  ->  1  RPC transport
  grep -ohE '"omp/[a-zA-Z]+"' dist/cli.js | sort -u              ->  3  omp/* methods

THE 57 DIRECTORIES, verbatim: advisor async auto-thinking autolearn autoresearch blob-broker capability cleanse cli collab commands commit compress config dap debug discovery edit eval exa exec export extensibility goals hindsight if-bench internal-urls irc jsonrpc launch lib live lsp markit mcp memories memory-backend mnemopi modes plan-mode registry secrets security session sharpshooter slash-commands ssh stt subprocess task tiny tools tts tui utils vibe web

THE NUMERATOR TODAY: ZERO. Measured across every crate's src -- Command::new("omp") 0 files, mode=rpc 0, muxConnect 0, omp/ 0. What we actually spawn: br 5 sites, git 4, tmux 1, cargo 1. The orchestrator named omp-orchestrator does not speak to OMP; it types into OMP's terminal and reads OMP's status line.

WHY THIS IS THE MISSION AND NOT A REFACTOR: every classifier defect measured today is downstream of having no protocol. Pane state comes from a braille spinner regex because there is no state RPC. "Receiver receipt" is a timer reset plus a spinner-stripped content hash because there is no delivery response. Two panes read `<no marker>` because a tool-call box border renders AFTER the status line -- an artifact that cannot exist over a typed protocol. ntm refuses codex panes with "cod composer not visible" (cp-nq2s9), a terminal-inspection guard rather than a protocol error. cp-z42vu returned success:[4] while the packet never arrived, and the inverse fired the same day in the pending-dispatch marker. Both polarities are the signature of an unacknowledged transport.

PER-CRATE CONTRACT -- every crate under this epic satisfies ALL of it, and each clause has a measured reason from this repo:
1. ASUPERSYNC-NATIVE. &Cx first in every async API; cx.checkpoint() in loops, retries, long handlers; region-owned tasks via Cx::spawn/Scope, no detached tasks. Kill the process GROUP, never the pid -- measured: orphaned grandchildren at ppid=1, 0.0% CPU, still holding the admission lock, so every timeout guaranteed the next attempt failed too.
2. MEMORY-SAFE. unsafe_code = "forbid". A crate that will not compile under the lint is a FINDING, not a reason to drop the lint. Today 14 of 20 carry it.
3. CANCEL-CORRECT. A timeout is not a verdict: a killed child's empty stdout maps to TIMEOUT, never to the token a genuinely failing subject produces. Drain both pipes -- piping stdout and stderr then polling try_wait() deadlocks past ~64 KiB; the tell is 0% CPU with no children, so widening the timeout makes it worse. Use subprocess-contract::run_output.
4. TYPED. Every state an enum with an exhaustive match, so a new variant is a compile error rather than a silent fallthrough. Measured: an earlier decide() derived free_capacity from the same filter as dispatchable, which made the NewlyIdle branch UNREACHABLE and let the fleet sit idle while every watchdog reported healthy.
5. LOGGED. One typed row per step, and the step count is ASSERTED. Measured: the supervisor emitted a byte-identical refusal for 29 consecutive ticks and nobody read it; 29 copies of one sentence carry no state.
6. OBSERVABLE. Every field has its OWN predicate and an explicit UNKNOWN. A field must never be derived from another field's filter, and an unmatched pattern must never collapse into a verdict -- both failures happened today (free_capacity: [] beside two IDLE panes; `<no marker>` beside two working panes).
7. ROBOT-REACHABLE. Per /agent-ergonomics-and-intuitiveness-maximization-for-cli-tools and /canonical-cli-scoping: doctor/health/repair triad, versioned JSON envelope, namespaced probe ids, idempotent repair, structured output. An agent must answer "what is true right now" in ONE command with no prose parsing.
8. WIRED. A caller exists and a conformance test proves it, with an EMPTY UNWIRED_LANE_ALLOWANCE where an exception is a named row with a reason. Measured: 12 of 20 crates currently have no path to execution, and BUILT != WIRED occurred eighteen times in a single session.

THE JOURNEY THIS SERVES -- idea to shipped, with the skill that governs each stage and the OMP surface it should ride:
  plan      /planning-workflow          plan-mode, modes, goals
  beads     /beads-workflow             task, commands, slash-commands
  triage    /beads-bv                   registry, capability, discovery
  dispatch  /vibing-with-ntm            irc, collab, jsonrpc, mcp, launch, exec, subprocess
  observe   /ntm-fleet-monitor          session, live, tui
  verify    /brennerbot-with-ntm        eval, if-bench, hindsight, debug, dap
  close     typed receipt               commit, export, memories

ACCEPTANCE FOR THE EPIC:
1. A checked-in coverage table with one row per surface: surface | what it provides | crate that owns it | asupersync/typed/logged/observable/robot/wired columns | classification (a) not ours, (b) reimplemented by scraping, (c) unused capability we should adopt.
2. COVERAGE IS A RATIO WITH A NAMED DENOMINATOR AND A RE-RUNNABLE COMMAND. "100%" with an unstated denominator is the 81-of-17 failure repeating: AGENTS.md asserted "81 JSON-RPC methods, we use 17" and that figure could not be re-derived -- 3 omp/* methods and 39 subcommands were found instead. Retire inherited numbers; publish the command.
3. POSITIVE CONTROL: at least one surface must come back FULLY COVERED before the table is trustworthy. A table where everything is uncovered is indistinguishable from a broken scan.
4. ANTI-VACUITY: an empty surface enumeration is an ERROR, never "nothing to map".
5. Children are WAVES grouped by lifecycle stage, not 57 individual beads. 17+ beads in one wave is O(n^2) coordination; cap each wave at 3-5 concurrent.

NO-CLAIM 1: "zero consumed" is measured for OUR crates only. NTM may itself speak an OMP protocol beneath --robot-send; that is UNMEASURED. The evidence leans against it -- composer-visibility phrasing, timer-reset receipts -- but leaning is not measuring.
NO-CLAIM 2: mapping a surface is not adopting it. Some scraping may be correct because no alternative exists for third-party panes. The table's job is to make the choice VISIBLE, not to force a rewrite. A surface classified (a) not-ours is a legitimate terminal state and must be reachable without argument.
NO-CLAIM 3: 100% COVERAGE OF THE MAP IS NOT 100% CORRECTNESS. Static reachability proves a caller exists, never that a lane ran. tick-monitor had two manifest callers and a live process and still starved the fleet for 4.5 hours.

title: FrankenMermaid inventory map: every crate's inputs, outputs, invariant, and negative evidence — generated, never drawn
description:
WHAT: a single generated inventory map — a FrankenMermaid diagram plus the table behind it — showing how every crate interacts: inputs, outputs, what must be true for it to be correct, and the negative evidence that would refute it. Josh: "don't let unknown crates or surfaces creep in and stay in without challenging the use and purpose of every moving part."

WHY NOW: the repo has 20 crates and 12 OF THEM HAVE NO PATH TO EXECUTION (measured 2026-08-31 via cargo metadata reverse edges: 2 libraries with zero callers, 3 bins installed with no trigger, 7 bins neither installed nor triggered). Two crates were RETIRED today after being built, tested, and found to have no inbound edge. `finding` — written so that "a named gap is an obligation" would be representable — shipped with exactly one manifest caller, and that caller (finding-dispatch) itself has zero. A crate reachable only from dead code is furniture.

GENERATED, NEVER DRAWN. The diagram is emitted by a crate from measured edges. A hand-drawn diagram is a claim; a generated one is a measurement. Sources, in order of authority:
  1. `cargo metadata --no-deps` reverse dependency edges — the compile-time graph. AUTHORITATIVE for lib->lib.
  2. Runtime triggers — git hooks, launchd, crontab, ~/.local/bin — for bin crates, whose "caller" is not a manifest edge.
  3. Spawn census — `Command::new("...")` per crate — for process-boundary edges the manifest cannot show.
NEVER grep crate names to infer edges: a census that greps names matches its own table. That is the self-referential checker, SIX instances in one session, and it produced a reading where all six gates falsely appeared to have callers.

EVERY NODE CARRIES FOUR FIELDS, and a node missing any of them is itself the finding:
  INPUTS   — what it consumes, and from whom
  OUTPUTS  — what it produces, and who consumes it (empty = the finding)
  MUST BE TRUE — the invariant that makes it correct. Not a description; a falsifiable claim.
  NEGATIVE EVIDENCE — the observation that would REFUTE it. Per /brennerbot-with-ntm: prefer refuters over supporters; evidence that could kill the hypothesis is worth more than evidence consistent with it. A node whose negative evidence is "none" is unfalsifiable and must be flagged.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. GENERATED FROM `cargo metadata` + trigger scan + spawn census, emitted as a mermaid graph AND a table. Re-runnable by one command whose output is pasted beside the diagram.
2. EVERY CRATE APPEARS, including the ones with no edges — an isolated node is the most important thing on the diagram. A crate silently absent is indistinguishable from a crate with no edges, which is the exact failure this bead exists to end.
3. ORPHAN CLASS IS EXPLICIT: nodes with zero inbound edges AND no runtime trigger render distinctly and are listed separately with a required disposition per crate — WIRE, RETIRE, or a named reason to keep. No fourth option. Today that list is 12 of 20.
4. POSITIVE CONTROL: `subprocess-contract` (3 manifest callers) and `no-shell-gate` (triggered by .git/hooks/pre-commit, PROVEN to refuse a staged .sh at exit 1) must render as connected/triggered. If everything renders orphaned the generator is broken, and a broken generator is indistinguishable from a dead repo.
5. FIRES-ON-KNOWN-BAD: add a crate with no callers; it appears in the orphan class and the check exits nonzero. Ship the specimen IN-TREE — an external apply-patch harness silently no-ops when its index hash misses HEAD.
6. ANTI-VACUITY: zero crates discovered is an ERROR, never a clean diagram.
7. THE FOUR FIELDS ARE MANDATORY PER NODE. A node with an empty MUST-BE-TRUE or NEGATIVE-EVIDENCE field fails the check. This is the clause that stops the map decaying into a picture.
8. MUTATION: delete one real edge from the input; the diagram must change and the orphan count must rise. Restore byte-identically, report the sha both sides.

COMPOSES WITH, DOES NOT DUPLICATE: crate-reachability-census-44g computes reachability; unwired-lane-conformance-6cd fails the build on an unwired lane; omp-surface-map-41b maps OMP surfaces to crates. This bead is the RENDERING and the FOUR-FIELD DISCIPLINE over those three. Consume their output; do not recompute it. If any of the three is not yet landed, emit the diagram with that column marked UNMEASURED rather than guessing — an honest gap beats a confident fill.

NO-CLAIM: a diagram proves structure, never behaviour. Static edges show that a caller EXISTS, not that a lane RAN — tick-monitor had two manifest callers and a live process and still starved the fleet for 4.5 hours. And a generated diagram inherits its generator's blind spots: if the spawn census misses a dynamically-constructed command name, that edge is invisible and the map will look complete while being wrong. State the generator's known blind spots ON the diagram.
close_reason: DONE: generated machine-readable inventory map is implemented and verified; live slash metadata remains explicitly UNKNOWN rather than a false pass.

  drop one declaration        -> FAIL, names `no-shell-gate`

  EMPTY SCAN SET              -> PASS   <-- DEFECT IN MY DEMONSTRATION

MY PROSE VALIDATOR FAILS ANTI-VACUITY. Feed it an empty crate set and an empty declaration set and it reports PASS. That is the exact clause this repo requires of every gate — an empty scan set is an ERROR, never a pass, because a deliverable that was never checked reports identically to one that passed. I found it only by running the leg against my own check, and I am handing it to you as a REQUIRED known-bad rather than leaving it in a commit message where it would rot:

  YOUR IMPLEMENTATION MUST FAIL ON: zero crates discovered, zero declarations parsed, or an
  unreadable/missing OMP-SURFACE-MAP.toml. All three are ERRORS, none of them is a clean pass.

POSITIVE CONTROL for the new axis, so a gate that flags everything cannot masquerade as working: `no-shell-gate` must come back declared "a" and `tick-monitor` must come back declared "b" with a non-empty `omp_alternative`.

NO-CLAIM: a declaration is a CLAIM BY THE AUTHOR, not a measurement. A crate can declare "a" and be wrong — `finding-dispatch` declares "a" and simultaneously carries the note that it has ZERO callers while being omp-orchestrator's only manifest caller, which is a WIRE-or-RETIRE decision this file records but does not make. The census's job is to make the claim exist and be challengeable. Adjudication is the inventory map, ipg.12, with its four mandatory fields.

title: One-touch install: Rust installer crate, four-way identity proof, standing drift check
description:
WHAT: a one-touch install that keeps the latest binary built, installed, and PROVEN to be the one running. Per /installer-workmanship, adapted to this repo's first rule.

THE CONFLICT, RESOLVED EXPLICITLY RATHER THAN IGNORED. /installer-workmanship's deliverable is `install.sh` and names DCG's and RCH's installers as the gold standard. THIS REPO'S ONE RULE IS: no `.sh`, no `.py`, exemption list empty by design. That rule is not aspirational — `.git/hooks/pre-commit` is a Mach-O binary and I proved it refuses a staged `.sh` with exit 1 and a named refusal. A tracked `install.sh` here is not a style disagreement; it cannot be committed.

RESOLUTION, following this repo's own precedent — every shell thing became Rust: ack-detector.sh -> ack.rs, heartbeat-check.sh -> heartbeat.rs, the four cron lanes -> three Rust crates.
  * THE INSTALLER IS A RUST CRATE. Platform detection, preflight, atomic lock, checksum, extract, install -m 0755, completions, agent config, summary, uninstall — all of it, in Rust, satisfying the eight mission clauses like every other crate.
  * THE CURL ENTRY POINT IS A GENERATED RELEASE ARTIFACT, NOT A TRACKED FILE. `curl | bash` is irreducibly shell — you cannot pipe curl into a Rust binary. So the bootstrap is the SMALLEST POSSIBLE shell: detect platform, fetch the installer binary, exec it. It is EMITTED by the installer crate into the release artifact and never committed, so `git ls-files | grep -E '\.(sh|py)$'` stays at 0 and the gate stays green.
  * NO-CLAIM ON THAT SPLIT: the bootstrap is still shell, still unverified at the moment it runs, and still the weakest link. Moving 95% of the logic into Rust shrinks the blast radius; it does not eliminate it. Anyone claiming this repo has "no shell in the install path" is wrong — it has the least shell that the transport permits, and the bootstrap must therefore be short enough to audit in one screen.

WHY NOW, MEASURED 2026-08-31:
  HEAD = 94ac507. Installed supervisor = build_id 9a61acd. TWENTY-THREE COMMITS BEHIND.
  The launchd job has been running a stale binary for hours, through the entire gate-census
  landing. This is the source == installed == running failure the session catalogued EIGHT times,
  live right now, on the one binary that supervises everything else.
  There is NO install path tracked in the repo at all: `git ls-files | grep -iE 'install|bootstrap|setup'` returns NOTHING.
  `tick-monitor --version` DOES NOT EXIST — it prints usage. One of the two installed binaries has no version surface, so its identity CANNOT be established by any means short of hashing the file against a build we still have. That is a hard blocker for any install that claims to verify itself.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. ONE COMMAND installs from clean. Its output names the resolved version, the target triple, the install path, and the verified identity.
2. IDENTITY IS PROVEN AT INSTALL TIME, not asserted. The four-way check this session established as the standard: `git rev-parse HEAD` == the `build_id` in the artifact's `strings` == what `--version` reports == what the running process reports via its heartbeat. Install FAILS if the four disagree. Measured precedent: a build started at 09a1da4, HEAD reached 85828bf, and the installed binary reported build_id f94ea53 — three identities for one artifact, because three commits landed inside three minutes.
3. EVERY INSTALLED BINARY HAS `--version` EMITTING `build_id`. tick-monitor does not today, and until it does, its identity leg is UNMEASURABLE, not merely unmeasured. Add it as part of this bead.
4. IT REFUSES TO INSTALL WHILE A BUILD IS REGISTERED IN FLIGHT, reusing commit-build-fence (closed, 6+4 legs, mutation proven through the real hook). Do not reimplement the registration; consume it.
5. FIRES-ON-KNOWN-BAD: hand it an artifact whose build_id disagrees with HEAD; it REFUSES and names both. Hand it a corrupted tarball; the SHA256 check fails and names the expected and actual digests.
6. KNOWN-GOOD, mandatory: a clean matching install SUCCEEDS and the four identities agree. Without this leg the installer could refuse everything and look identical to a working one.
7. ANTI-VACUITY: zero artifacts found is an ERROR, never "nothing to install".
8. THE DRIFT CHECK IS A STANDING SURFACE, not a one-shot: one robot command answers "is what is running the same as what is committed?" and exits nonzero when it is not. Per /canonical-cli-scoping and /agent-ergonomics: doctor/health/repair, versioned JSON envelope, namespaced probe ids. An agent must get that answer in ONE command with no prose parsing.
9. MUTATION: break the identity comparison; leg 2 goes RED. Restore byte-identically, sha both sides.

ADOPT FROM THE REFERENCE INSTALLERS, translated to Rust: 4-tier artifact fallback then build-from-source; dual checksum tooling; proxy support on every fetch; atomic mkdir-based locking with stale-PID detection; already-installed short-circuit that STILL reconfigures; per-agent status in the final summary; uninstall instructions always printed. Skip nothing on the grounds that this repo is internal — the one-touch claim is the deliverable.

NO-CLAIM: an installer that verifies identity at install time does NOT keep it true afterwards. The next commit makes the running binary stale again, which is precisely today's 23-commit gap. Continuous truth needs the standing drift check of clause 8 wired into the supervisor's own tick, and even then a check is not a rebuild — it reports drift, it does not close it.

WHAT EXISTS: the four-way identity check (HEAD == build_id in artifact strings == --version output == running process), the build-in-flight fence (refuses installing during a concurrent build), the install-and-rollback-on-mismatch path, and the workspace release builder.

The build-in-flight fence REUSES the closed commit-build-fence contract (6+4 legs, mutation proven through the real hook). It does not reimplement the registration.

comments.author: josh
comments.text:
GRADE: REFUSED by orchestrator (pane 1), non-author. One reason, and it is the whole bead.

THE BINARY INSTALLS NOTHING AND EXITS 0.

  $ installer
  installer: not yet wired to the live fleet
  $ echo $?
  0

crates/installer/src/main.rs, all eleven lines, is:

  fn main() -> ExitCode {
      println!("installer: not yet wired to the live fleet");
      ExitCode::SUCCESS
  }

THIS IS A RETIRED PATTERN, NOT A NEW ONE. Earlier today `dispatch-actuation` printed the byte-identical string — "dispatch-actuation: not yet wired to the live fleet" — returned exit 0, and was RETIRED on Josh's judgement for exactly this. The same shape has now shipped a second time in one session, in the crate whose acceptance clause 1 reads "ONE COMMAND installs from clean."

WHY EXIT 0 MAKES IT WORSE THAN AN ERROR. A no-op that reports failure is a stub. A no-op that reports SUCCESS is a false green: a caller, a CI lane, or a human reads 0 as "installed". That is the same family as three defects measured today — `br comment` (singular) printing a usage error on stderr and EXITING 0 so an agent believed two VERDICT comments had landed when neither had; `cargo` returning exit 103 with 0 passed 0 failed, which I myself briefly read as a test result rather than a refusal; and ntm returning success:[4] while the packet never arrived. In every case the exit code lied and only a read-back caught it. An installer that exits 0 without installing will be trusted by something.

WHAT IS GENUINELY GOOD, and it is most of the work: 325 lines of lib.rs, 3 tests passing, exit 0 on `cargo test -p installer`; the four-way identity design is right; the build-in-flight fence correctly REUSES the closed commit-build-fence contract rather than reimplementing registration; and the curl bootstrap is a release artifact that is never committed, which keeps `git ls-files | grep -E '\.(sh|py)$'` at ZERO — I verified that, and it resolves the /installer-workmanship conflict with this repo's one rule exactly as the bead specified. None of that is in question.

THE GAP IS THE LAST INCH: `main` does not call `lib`. 325 lines of correct logic with no production caller is the nineteenth BUILT != WIRED of this session, and this one is self-inflicted by a `main` that was written to compile rather than to run.

TO CLOSE:
1. `main` invokes the real path. `installer --check` (or the bare command) performs the four-way identity comparison against the live system and exits NONZERO on drift.
2. FIRES-ON-KNOWN-BAD THROUGH THE REAL BINARY, and you have a live specimen requiring no fixture: the installed supervisor is `build_id 9a61acd` while HEAD is well past it — TWENTY-THREE COMMITS at the time I measured. Run your binary against that and it must REFUSE and NAME both identities. If it prints anything resembling success, the leg has not fired.
3. KNOWN-GOOD, mandatory: after a real install where the four agree, the same command exits 0. Without this leg the installer could refuse everything and look identical to a working one.
4. ANTI-VACUITY: an unreadable `--version`, a missing binary, or an unresolvable HEAD is an ERROR, never a clean pass. Relevant immediately — `tick-monitor --version` DOES NOT EXIST; it prints usage. Its identity is UNMEASURABLE, not merely unmeasured, and the bead requires you to add the version surface.
5. Its own conformance row is a finding you should close in the same pass: `installer` has FIVE raw `Command::new` sites and does NOT depend on `subprocess-contract`. Per ASUPERSYNC-CONFORMANCE.md (commit 3e034f7) those are five potential undrained-pipe deadlock sites in the crate whose entire job is spawning build and install commands. The tell is 0% CPU with no children, and widening the timeout makes it worse.

NO-CLAIM on this refusal: I did not run the install path end to end, because there is no install path to run. If `main` had called `lib` and the identity check had failed for a real reason, that would be a different and much better conversation.

comments.author: SilverWolf
comments.text:
IPG.13 — the deciding leg is PROVEN (SilverWolf, pane 5, %1409). main is wired to the real path and the live system proves it.

The installer binary --check against the live system:
  HEAD=3f8c41e
  omp-orchestrator: HEAD=3f8c41e... build_id= version=9a61acd MISMATCH

comments.author: josh
comments.text:
DECIDING LEG VERIFIED by orchestrator (pane 1), non-author. Re-ran your binary against the live system rather than reading your report. The refusal I posted an hour ago is WITHDRAWN as to the last inch — `main` now calls `lib`, and it fires.

  $ installer --check
  installer --check: HEAD=9be3558
    omp-orchestrator: HEAD=9be3558... build_id=        version=9a61acd  MISMATCH
    tick-monitor:     HEAD=9be3558... build_id=ABSENT  version=ABSENT   MISMATCH
    pane-truth:       HEAD=9be3558... build_id=ABSENT  version=ABSENT   MISMATCH

  $ echo $?

WHY THIS IS A REAL LEG AND NOT A FIXTURE: it fired against the ACTUAL installed state, and the drift it names is the one I measured independently before you started — the supervisor running build_id 9a61acd, 23+ commits behind. No planted input, no harness. The known-bad had a live specimen because the repo IS the specimen.

THREE THINGS THE OUTPUT DOES RIGHT, each worth naming because each is a place this class usually fails:

STILL OPEN ON THIS BEAD, unchanged by this verification:

  * installer has FIVE raw Command::new sites and no subprocess-contract dependency — five potential undrained-pipe deadlock sites in the crate whose whole job is spawning builds and installs. Per ASUPERSYNC-CONFORMANCE.md (3e034f7). The tell is 0% CPU with no children, and widening the timeout makes it worse.

NO-CLAIM: I verified DRIFT DETECTION. I did not verify INSTALLATION — nothing was installed during this check, by design. An installer that correctly refuses is not yet an installer that correctly installs, and only the blocked known-good leg can establish the second.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
A DEFECT I FOUND WHILE GRADING, AND IT IS STRUCTURAL, NOT COSMETIC.

So the check is comparing a control-plane artifact's identity against an omp-orchestrator commit.
Those two histories are unrelated. `pane-truth: MISMATCH` is not a drift report — it is a
CATEGORY ERROR, and it will read MISMATCH forever no matter how correct every install becomes.

That matters beyond neatness for two reasons:
1. IT POISONS THE KNOWN-GOOD LEG YOU STILL OWE. "After a real install where the four agree, the
   command exits 0" is UNREACHABLE while a permanently-mismatched row is in the set. You would be

2. THE 3/3 HEADLINE OVERSTATES. Two binaries have real, closable drift. The third has an

title: Mine the mirror before declaring anything hard — asupersync already solved our receipt gap
description:
WHAT: a standing discipline plus its first payoff. Josh, 2026-08-31: "make sure we are mining — diligently — every gap that says 'we don't know how to do this, or this is hard' — the dicklesworthstone-mirror for examples of how to do it right. He pushes so much work and has so many projects to reference, that it's not possible to have any gaps in next-gen approaches to any hard things."

THE RULE: before writing "UNMEASURED", "hard", "no alternative exists", or inventing a mechanism, SEARCH THE MIRROR. 216 repos at /Volumes/ZestData/dicklesworthstone-mirror. `fh suggest` is the index; when `fh serve` reports SERVE_INPUT_STALE (mirror HEAD moved), grep the mirror directly rather than treating the gap as unanswered — a stale index means the answer is unindexed, not absent.

THE FIRST PAYOFF, and it refutes three of our own designs. Our hardest open gap was stated on OMP-SURFACE-MAP.toml revision 2 as: "OMP provides NO delivery receipt. The receiver-verification gap is REAL and CANNOT be closed by adopting an OMP surface." That is true about OMP and it is NOT true about the problem. Searching the mirror for delivery-receipt prior art returns, first hit, asupersync/src/messaging/fabric.rs — OUR OWN BINDING DEPENDENCY, which we already require in every crate, and which solved this properly.

WHAT IT HAS THAT WE REINVENTED WORSE:

1. AckKind — "Acknowledgement boundary reached by the operation" (fabric.rs:1919, on PublishReceipt). A TYPED BOUNDARY, not a boolean and not three parallel authorities. We invented a three-authority ack spine — transport success, observational delivery, bead-comment ack — precisely because we had no vocabulary for "how far did this get". AckKind IS that vocabulary. messaging/class.rs:59-62 maps each delivery class to its boundary: EphemeralInteractive -> one kind, DurableOrdered -> Recoverable, ObligationBacked -> Ser(vice?), MobilitySafe/ForensicReplayable -> another.

2. DeliveryClass (messaging/class.rs:17-29) — five semantic classes: EphemeralInteractive (default, hot pub/sub, no durability), DurableOrdered, ObligationBacked (request/reply and service flows), MobilitySafe (safe across stewardship change), ForensicReplayable (replay-heavy reasoning tier). WE HAVE NO DELIVERY CLASS AT ALL. Every dispatch packet is treated identically, which is why a fence was needed to stop retries — an ephemeral nudge and a bead assignment carry the same weight in our system and they should not.

3. PublishPermit (fabric.rs:1944) — two-phase reservation, and the line that matters:
     #[must_use = "a PublishPermit must be sent or explicitly aborted"]
     "Dropping without calling either method aborts cleanly (no data committed, no obligation leaked)."
   THAT IS THE PENDING-DISPATCH FENCE, SOLVED. Our marker sat for 29 CONSECUTIVE TICKS because nothing owned its release and no drop path aborted it. A permit that aborts on drop cannot leak. Our Duty type has #[must_use] but no two-phase reservation and no ledger, so a dropped Duty leaks an obligation that only a human notices.

4. ObligationLedger / ObligationToken / ObligationId — obligations are RESERVED, then committed or aborted, against a ledger. Our Finding crate exists to make "a named gap is an obligation" representable and shipped with zero callers. asupersync already has the ledger.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. A MINING PASS over every current UNMEASURED / "hard" / "no alternative" claim in this repo's beads and docs, each answered with either a mirror citation (repo, path, line) or an explicit "searched, not found" naming the search. "Searched and not found" is a legitimate result; SILENCE IS NOT.
2. The receipt design specifically: re-derive ack-spine against asupersync's AckKind + DeliveryClass + PublishPermit before writing more of it. Either adopt them, or state with the measurement why a pane-dispatch boundary cannot use them.
3. FIRES-ON-KNOWN-BAD: a bead containing "UNMEASURED" or "we don't know" with no adjacent mirror citation or explicit not-found is FLAGGED. Ship the specimen in-tree.
4. POSITIVE CONTROL: at least one gap must come back genuinely NOT FOUND in the mirror, or the search is matching everything and proves nothing.
5. ANTI-VACUITY: zero gaps enumerated is an ERROR, never "no gaps".

NO-CLAIM 1: asupersync's fabric is a MESSAGING plane between components that both use it. Whether its permit/ack machinery can wrap a tmux pane that has never heard of asupersync is UNMEASURED — that is the very first thing to test, and it may come back (a) not applicable. The finding is that we invented vocabulary that already exists, not that adoption is proven.
NO-CLAIM 2: `fh serve` was STALE at the time of this search (SERVE_INPUT_STALE, mirror HEAD moved from 5dec4212 to ecdea397). These hits came from a direct grep, so the ranked index may surface better prior art once restarted. Re-run through fh before treating this list as complete.

title: Generate the asupersync conformance table and triage all 29 raw spawn sites
description:
WHAT: turn ASUPERSYNC-CONFORMANCE.md from a hand-taken snapshot into a generated, enforced gate — and close the two findings it exposed.

THE SCHEMA IS LANDED (commit 3e034f7). Eight greppable properties per crate: forbid_unsafe, dep_asupersync, dep_subprocess_contract, async_fns, cx_first, checkpoints, raw_command, forbidden_deps. Measured across 22 crates.

FINDING 1 — 29 RAW `Command::new` SITES, 4 CRATES USING THE DRAIN-SAFE RUNNER.
Every raw site is a potential undrained-pipe deadlock. The measured failure: piping stdout AND stderr then polling `try_wait()` deadlocks past ~64 KiB, and THE TELL IS 0% CPU WITH NO CHILDREN — a slow computation burns CPU, a deadlock does not, so widening the timeout makes it WORSE. A `git log` taking 0.9s from a shell sat at 0.0% CPU for 104s as a child.
`undrained-pipe-lint` exists to find exactly these and has ZERO CALLERS. Twenty-nine sites have never been scanned by the lint written for them. That is the sharpest BUILT != WIRED instance in the repo: not a lint with no findings, a lint with 29 unexamined candidates.

FINDING 2 — THE CANCELLATION CONTRACT COVERS 27% OF THE WORKSPACE.
6 of 22 crates depend on asupersync. The other 16 have no `Cx`, so "cancel-correct" is not FALSE of them — it is UNREPRESENTABLE. AGENTS.md and README describe the contract as binding. Either the contract is scoped to the crates that spawn work and says so, or the 16 adopt it. Both are defensible; silence is not.

FINDING 3 — `pane-dispatch-fence` and `subprocess-contract` DEPEND ON ASUPERSYNC WHILE OMITTING `unsafe_code = "forbid"`. That combination is the least defensible on the board: they carry the runtime contract and skip the memory-safety lint. Six crates lack the lint in total.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. GENERATED, NEVER DRAWN. A crate emits the table on every run. The current file is a snapshot with a timestamp, which per the inventory-map doctrine is a measurement and not a gate. Print the command beside the output.
2. FIRES-ON-KNOWN-BAD: add a crate with a raw `Command::new` and no `subprocess-contract` dependency; the gate NAMES it. Ship the specimen IN-TREE — an external apply-patch harness silently no-ops when its index hash misses HEAD.
3. POSITIVE CONTROL, mandatory: `omp-orchestrator` (8 async fns, 8 cx-first, 3 checkpoints, asupersync + subprocess-contract) must report CONFORMANT. A gate that flags everything is indistinguishable from a broken one, and this repo has produced that reading twice today.
4. ANTI-VACUITY: zero crates scanned is an ERROR, never a clean report. Zero `Command::new` sites found is ALSO an error while 29 are known present — that is a live regression canary for the scanner itself.
5. THE 29 SITES GET TRIAGED, each to one of: routed through `subprocess-contract`, or DEADLOCK-SAFE with the reason stated (stdout-only piping, or `wait_with_output()` with no poll loop, both of which are genuinely safe). "Not yet looked at" is not a category.
6. MUTATION: break the `raw_command` regex; leg 2 goes RED. Restore byte-identically, report the sha both sides.

DO NOT LET THE SCHEMA IMPLY MORE THAN IT MEASURES. Five NO-CLAIMs are on the file and must survive into the generator's output:
  * every column is SYNTACTIC — `cx_first` counts a parameter name, not honoured cancellation
  * `raw_command` is a LOWER BOUND — a dynamically-constructed command name is invisible
  * region ownership, kill-the-process-GROUP, timeout-is-not-a-verdict, Budget/Outcome/capability
    narrowing, two-phase effects and deterministic LabRuntime tests are ABSENT FROM THE SCHEMA
    because they are not greppable. They need a semantic pass and are named so their absence from
    the table is not read as absence from the contract.

VERSION DISCIPLINE: we pin `rev = "fa3c01aec"`; the mirror is at exactly that rev, version 0.4.9. The asupersync-mega-skill states v0.4.4 — stale relative to what we pin, and the skill's own live-doc rule says trust the live source over the skill. Any conformance claim must name the rev it was measured against, because the contract is version-pinned.

NO-CLAIM: a conformance table proves SHAPE, never BEHAVIOUR. A crate can score 8/8 and still leak a detached task, kill a pid instead of a process group, or map a timeout to the same token a genuinely failing subject produces. Those are the three failures that actually cost us time this session, and none of them is greppable.

title: PORTING CONTRACT: nothing lands unwired — and AGENTS.md documents 17 crates that are not here
description:
WHAT: the porting contract. Josh, 2026-08-31: "we need to get all work moved to this repo but following our proper porting process and gated ecosystem — nothing gets ported without wired, nothing gets a gate pass."

THE MEASUREMENT THAT REFRAMES THE PROJECT, taken 2026-08-31:

  crates here                     24
  crates in control-plane         59
  crates in BOTH                   4   composer-typed, fleet-composite, loop-queue-filter,
                                       pane-dispatch-fence
  crates in control-plane ONLY    55

  OF THE 20 CRATES AGENTS.md DOCUMENTS AS "the crates: what each one is and why it exists":
    3 ARE PRESENT      pane-dispatch-fence, composer-typed, loop-queue-filter
   17 ARE ABSENT       pane-truth, fleet-truth, fleet-reconcile, oracle-compare, pane-oracle-diff,
                       pane-dispatch-ready, ntm-fleet-monitor, loop-coverage, refill-idle-panes,
                       fast-dispatch, tick-dispatch, loop-driver, loop-tick, fleet-monitor,
                       verify-dispatch, dispatcher-deadman, reap-finished-panes

THE CRATE TABLE IN AGENTS.md DESCRIBES A REPOSITORY THAT DOES NOT EXIST. It carries a caveat that the descriptions were derived from Cargo.toml rather than from reading the source — it does NOT say the crates are not here. Every agent that has read AGENTS.md this session has been reasoning about seventeen crates that are in another repo.

AND THE EXTRACTION HAS NOT BEEN HAPPENING. Of the 24 crates here, 20 were BUILT FRESH in this repo during this session; only 4 came from control-plane. We have been writing new code beside an unported substrate, which is why `pane-truth` is INSTALLED on this machine from control-plane's tree while `crates/pane-truth` does not exist here — an artifact on PATH whose source lives in a repo with an unrelated history (control-plane HEAD 407ecb5 vs ours).

THE GATE — NOTHING PORTS WITHOUT WIRED, NOTHING GETS A PASS. A crate arrives only when ALL of the following are true IN THE SAME COMMIT. Any one absent means the crate does not land.

  1. WIRED. A production caller exists and a conformance test proves it reaches the crate. The
     UNWIRED_LANE_ALLOWANCE is EMPTY; an exception is a named row with a reason, not silence.
     THIS IS THE CLAUSE WITH THE MOST DEBT: 12 of the crates ALREADY HERE have no path to
     execution. The gate applies to arrivals; the existing 12 are tracked on
     crate-reachability-census-44g and are NOT grandfathered.
  2. SURFACE DECLARED. A `[crates.x]` block in OMP-SURFACE-MAP.toml with classification (a)/(b)/(c)
     and, for (b), the OMP alternative that EXISTS AND IS REACHABLE. UNDECLARED is a failure state.
  3. ASUPERSYNC CONFORMANCE ROW. All eight properties measured in ASUPERSYNC-CONFORMANCE.md.
     `forbid(unsafe_code)` is mandatory — a crate that will not compile under the lint is a
     FINDING, not a reason to drop the lint. Any `Command::new` routes through
     subprocess-contract or carries a stated deadlock-safe reason.
  4. REPOSITORY-GREEN, NOT TREE-GREEN. `git archive HEAD | tar -x` into a clean directory, then
     the crate's suite passes FROM THERE. Tree-green has hidden two real defects today:
     ack_detector passed 4/4 in-tree and 1/4 in-extract, and HEAD lacked `pub mod followup` while
     the working tree had it.
  5. NO `.sh`, NO `.py`. Enforced by the live pre-commit hook, proven to refuse a staged .sh at
     exit 1. A ported shell script is PORTED, not carried.
  6. FOUR FIELDS FOR THE INVENTORY MAP: inputs, outputs, what must be true, negative evidence. A
     node whose negative evidence is "none" is unfalsifiable and is flagged.

ORDER OF WORK, and it is not the order of the list above:
  FIRST correct AGENTS.md, because every agent is currently reasoning from a false crate table.
  SECOND port the leaves. 14 of the control-plane crates have zero path-dependencies and 6 have
  exactly one; leaves first is the only order that lets each arrival satisfy clause 1 without a
  forward reference.
  THIRD resolve pane-truth specifically — it is installed here, sourced there, and the installer's
  identity check reports it MISMATCH against a HEAD it can never match.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. AGENTS.md's crate table states, per row, whether the crate is HERE or IN CONTROL-PLANE. A reader must not be able to mistake an unported crate for a present one.
2. A porting checklist exists as a GATE, not a document — the six clauses above, machine-checked, refusing a landing that misses any.
3. FIRES-ON-KNOWN-BAD: attempt to land a crate with no caller; REFUSED, naming clause 1. Attempt one with no surface declaration; REFUSED, naming clause 2. Ship both specimens in-tree.
4. KNOWN-GOOD, mandatory: a correctly-ported crate lands unimpeded. A gate that refuses everything is indistinguishable from a broken one, and an over-strict gate gets routed around — which is a slower death than no gate.
5. ANTI-VACUITY: zero crates examined is an ERROR, never "nothing to port".

NO-CLAIM 1: 55 crates in control-plane are CANDIDATES, not a work queue. Some are cron-lane scaffolding that should die rather than move; the extraction set was variously stated as 20 and 23 and neither figure was ever derived. The denominator must be established before "how much is left" means anything — that is the same unstated-denominator defect as the retired "81 JSON-RPC methods, 17 used".
NO-CLAIM 2: the gate proves a crate ARRIVED wired. It cannot prove it STAYS wired — tick-monitor had two manifest callers and a live process and starved the fleet for 4.5 hours.

comments.author: josh
comments.text:
PORTING ORDER — measured authoritatively, 2026-08-31.

AGENTS.md says "14 leaves with zero path deps; 6 with exactly one. Extract leaves first."
That was scoped to the 20-crate set. Across ALL of control-plane, measured with
cargo metadata --no-deps (NOT grep):

  workspace members                     57
  TRUE leaves (zero intra-workspace dep) 34
  exactly one intra dep                  22
  two or more                             1

First twelve leaves, alphabetical: admission-reason, arc-keepalive, bughunt-tick,
cargo-lane-budget, check-publish, close-evidence-gate, composer-typed,
coordinator-reservation-preflight, crate-soundness-verify,
dispatch-chain-migration-check, dispatcher-deadman, fleet-composite.

A GREP GOT THIS WRONG FIRST, and the error is worth the line: grep -c 'path = "../'
over each Cargo.toml returned ONE leaf out of 59. The real answer is 34. Inline
table syntax escapes that pattern, and 'ls crates' also counted two non-crate
entries, which is why 59 appeared where 57 members exist.
This is the session's recurring confident-zero: a count that is real attached to a
predicate that does not match. cargo metadata cannot make that mistake because it
reads the resolved graph rather than the text.

WHY LEAVES FIRST IS NOT A PREFERENCE: clause 1 of this contract is WIRED — a
production caller plus a conformance test proving it reaches the crate, in the same
commit. A crate with an unported dependency cannot satisfy that without a forward
reference to something that does not exist yet. Leaves are the only arrivals that
can be born wired.

NO-CLAIM: 34 leaves is a DEPENDENCY fact, not a PRIORITY. Some leaves are cron-lane
scaffolding that should be retired rather than ported, and being a leaf says nothing
about whether the crate deserves to exist here. The kill-or-port decision is separate
and must be made per crate before any of them moves.

title: Type inventory: 51 enums, 79 structs, 4 collisions, 6 Verdict dialects, 4 types asupersync already has
description:
WHAT: the type inventory — a gated, generated list of every public type each crate owns, the collisions between them, and the types we are missing. Josh: "where is our list of types that we are managing, suggesting, and building, for all of the crates per our crate inventory ecosystem — gated in."

IT DID NOT EXIST. We gate the OMP surface per crate (OMP-SURFACE-MAP.toml) and the eight asupersync properties per crate (ASUPERSYNC-CONFORMANCE.md). Nothing has ever enumerated the TYPES, which is the layer where "typed, logged, observable" is actually delivered or not.

MEASURED 2026-08-31: 51 public enums, 79 public structs, across 22 of 24 crates.
Two crates own NO public type at all: finding-dispatch and pane-dispatch-fence — both already flagged elsewhere, finding-dispatch as a zero-caller library that is nevertheless omp-orchestrator's only manifest caller.

FINDING 1 — FOUR COLLIDING TYPE NAMES, and one of them is dangerous:
    Finding        finding, state-wildcard-lint
    LintReport     state-wildcard-lint, undrained-pipe-lint
    Violation      no-shell-gate, undrained-pipe-lint
    Observation    omp-orchestrator, tick-monitor      <-- THIS ONE
`Observation` is not a coincidental name clash. tick-monitor PRODUCES the observation that omp-orchestrator's `decide()` CONSUMES, and each defines its own incompatible struct. There is no shared type across the seam, so the producer and the consumer agree only by convention. That is exactly the seam where free_capacity was derived from the wrong filter and where a NewlyIdle pane became invisible as capacity — a defect that would have been a compile error if one type crossed the boundary.

FINDING 2 — SIX VERDICT TYPES, NO SHARED TRAIT:
    AckVerdict, FenceVerdict, FollowUpVerdict, ReceiptVerdict, SilenceVerdict, Verdict
Six independent answers to "what happened", none composable, none countable. This is precisely why grading is prose: there is no type a grade can BE, so a grade cannot be counted, queried, or required. Twelve beads currently sit in_progress with no verdict and nothing noticed, because nothing could.

FINDING 3 — SEVENTEEN TYPES IN THE ACK/RECEIPT VOCABULARY, SPLIT ACROSS TWO INCOMPATIBLE DIALECTS:
    ack-spine speaks AUTHORITY: TransportAuthority, DeliveryAuthority, AckAuthority, AckEvidence, AckSummary
    ack-stage speaks RECEIPT:   TransportReceipt, TransportReceiptError, AckReadback, AckStageInput/Result
    receiver-receipt speaks a third: ReceiptVerdict, ReceiptReason, PostSendObservation
Three crates, three vocabularies, one problem. They were written days apart by different agents against the same gap and never reconciled.

FINDING 4 — THE TYPES WE ARE MISSING, checked by name:
    Grade             ABSENT   <- the gap that makes grading prose
    DeliveryClass     ABSENT   <- asupersync has it: EphemeralInteractive/DurableOrdered/
                                  ObligationBacked/MobilitySafe/ForensicReplayable
    AckKind           ABSENT   <- asupersync has it: "acknowledgement boundary reached"
    ObligationLedger  ABSENT   <- asupersync has it: reserve, then commit or abort
    Budget            ABSENT
    Outcome           PRESENT, but only in tick-monitor and unrelated to asupersync's Outcome
Four of the six absent types ALREADY EXIST in asupersync at the rev we pin (fa3c01aec, v0.4.9). We invented three ack dialects for a vocabulary we already depend on.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. GENERATED, NEVER DRAWN. omp-inventory-map already exists and already models InventoryRow/Node/Edge — extend it to emit the type inventory rather than writing a second scanner. One command, output pasted beside it.
2. COLLISION DETECTION IS A GATE, NOT A REPORT: two crates declaring the same public type name FAILS, unless the row carries a named reason. Same shape as UNWIRED_LANE_ALLOWANCE — the allowance starts with the four measured entries above and each states why the duplication is acceptable or when it dies.
3. THE `Observation` COLLISION GETS A DECISION, not an allowance row: one shared type across the tick-monitor -> omp-orchestrator seam, or a stated reason why the producer and consumer must diverge. This is the highest-value single row in the inventory.
4. POSITIVE CONTROL: a crate with a unique, well-formed type set must PASS. A gate that flags all 22 is indistinguishable from a broken one.
5. ANTI-VACUITY: zero types discovered is an ERROR, never a clean inventory. Two crates legitimately own no public type; that must be reported as a NAMED ZERO, not silence.
6. THE MISSING-TYPE LIST IS PART OF THE OUTPUT. An inventory that lists only what exists cannot show a gap, and the gap is the point of this bead.
7. MUTATION: rename a type to collide deliberately; leg 2 goes RED and names both crates. Restore byte-identically, sha both sides.

NO-CLAIM 1: a type inventory proves SHAPE, not SEMANTICS. Two crates can own identically-named types that mean different things (Violation in no-shell-gate vs undrained-pipe-lint may be legitimately distinct), and two differently-named types can mean the same thing — which is exactly the ack/receipt case. The gate catches name collisions; a human decides whether the vocabulary is actually split.
NO-CLAIM 2: "ABSENT" was checked by exact name. A crate could implement DeliveryClass semantics under another name and this scan would call it absent. The four asupersync types are named from that codebase; adopting them is a separate decision, and mapping a surface is not adopting it.
close_reason: MUTATION-VERIFIED 8bf5edf: 13/13 tests, live gate REFUSES exactly the Observation seam with the CONVERGE decision row; generated inventory pasted; two bead-text corrections (Budget present-upstream, ObligationLedger absent-everywhere)

CONSUMPTION CONTRACT for ipg.18 (AmberGate): path-dep on omp-inventory-map; call scan_workspace_types + TypeInventory::check/ collsions/disallowed from her single cargo-test target; her legs 4/5 fixtures should be synthetic crates (the mutation pattern is in my tests) so allowance rows cannot silence her specimens. Coordination notice sent to %1414 at claim time; Agent Mail CLI is broken (symlink -> QUARANTINED binary) so the contract went over tmux — recorded here as the durable copy.

title: Five-leg conformance gate: make every per-crate declaration something cargo test refuses
description:
WHAT: one conformance test with five legs, so every per-crate declaration this repo has written becomes something `cargo test` REFUSES rather than something a document asserts.

THE MEASUREMENT THAT MAKES THIS P0, taken 2026-08-31: we have written four per-crate declarations and THREE OF THEM ARE READ BY NOTHING.

  ENFORCES (something refuses on violation):
    crates/no-shell-gate/tests/wired_lanes.rs   RED right now on "UNWIRED LANE: installer"
    .git/hooks/commit-msg                        Mach-O, MSG_SRC x5, refused the orchestrator's
                                                 own commit at 16:00
    .git/hooks/pre-commit                        enforces no-shell-gate ONLY
  DECLARES (no reader, no refusal):
    OMP-SURFACE-MAP.toml         consumed_by_code = 1
    ASUPERSYNC-CONFORMANCE.md    consumed_by_code = 0
    omp-types                    depended_on_by   = 0 of 25 crates

The canonical vocabulary shipped with ZERO dependents forty minutes after being written, by the orchestrator, in the session where that is the cardinal sin. It is available and mandatory nowhere. That is the twentieth BUILT != WIRED here and the reason this bead exists rather than a fifth document.

THE PATTERN TO COPY IS ALREADY IN THE TREE. `wired_lanes.rs` is the only proven enforcement in this repo and it has the right shape:
    fn every_declared_lane_has_a_production_caller()          <- the substantive leg
    fn every_allowance_row_names_a_lane_and_carries_a_reason() <- validates the EXCEPTIONS
The second function is the one most gates omit. Without it an allowance list degrades into a place to put things you do not want to fix.

THE FIVE LEGS, each with an allowance list that starts EMPTY and whose rows carry reasons:

  LEG 1  WIRED — exists, red on `installer`. Do not touch it; extend beside it.
  LEG 2  SURFACE DECLARED — every workspace crate has a [crates.x] block in OMP-SURFACE-MAP.toml.
         UNDECLARED (crate present, no block) and GHOST (block present, no crate) both FAIL.
         The input is validated 21/21 and already ships ONE DELIBERATE GHOST specimen
         (crates.ack-spine-collab-gap) so the GHOST leg fires on an in-tree case permanently.
  LEG 3  ASUPERSYNC CONFORMANCE — the eight properties. forbid(unsafe_code) is mandatory; six
         crates lack it today, and two of those (pane-dispatch-fence, subprocess-contract) carry
         the asupersync dependency while omitting the lint, which is the least defensible pair on
         the board. Every Command::new routes through subprocess-contract or carries a stated
         deadlock-safe reason: 29 raw sites exist against 4 compliant crates.
  LEG 4  CANONICAL TYPES — a crate declaring a public type that duplicates one re-exported by
         omp-types FAILS. This is the leg that makes the vocabulary mandatory instead of
         available, and without it omp-types stays furniture.
  LEG 5  NO COLLISIONS — two crates declaring the same public type name FAILS. Allowance seeded
         with the four measured rows: Finding, LintReport, Violation, Observation. `Observation`
         requires a DECISION, not an allowance row — tick-monitor produces what omp-orchestrator
         consumes and each declares its own incompatible struct, which is the seam where
         free_capacity was derived from the wrong filter and a NewlyIdle pane went invisible as
         capacity. One shared type makes that a compile error.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. All five legs live in ONE test target that runs under plain `cargo test`. Not a binary someone
   remembers to invoke — the distinguishing property of leg 1 is not that it is better written, it
   is that cargo refuses.
2. EVERY LEG HAS ITS OWN ALLOWANCE VALIDATOR, mirroring
   `every_allowance_row_names_a_lane_and_carries_a_reason`. An entry with an empty reason must fail
   the validator, so nobody can silence a leg with a bare path.
3. FIRES-ON-KNOWN-BAD, one specimen per leg, all IN-TREE: an unwired crate (have it), an undeclared
   crate, a crate missing forbid(unsafe_code), a crate redeclaring a canonical type, and a name
   collision. An external apply-patch harness silently no-ops when its index hash misses HEAD.
4. KNOWN-GOOD IS MANDATORY PER LEG: a conforming crate passes every leg untouched. Five legs is
   five times the chance of being over-strict, and an over-strict gate gets routed around, which
   is a slower death than no gate.
5. ANTI-VACUITY PER LEG: zero crates scanned is an ERROR for every leg independently. A shared
   scan that returns empty must not let five legs pass together.
6. MUTATION: break each leg's predicate in turn; that leg goes RED and the other four stay GREEN.
   If breaking one turns several red they share a defect and are not five legs.

NO-CLAIM 1: this makes nonconformance FAIL THE SUITE. It does not make it impossible — a leg can
be deleted, an allowance row added, or the suite skipped. It raises the floor from "a document
says so" to "removing the check is an explicit, reviewable act."
NO-CLAIM 2: legs 2 through 5 are CANDIDATE — specified, inputs measured, not built. Only leg 1 is
banked, and it is banked because it fired unprompted on a real lane. Do not describe this bead as
"the conformance gate" until at least one new leg has gone red on its own specimen.
NO-CLAIM 3: five green legs prove SHAPE, never BEHAVIOUR. A crate can satisfy all five and still
leak a detached task, kill a pid instead of a process group, or map a timeout to the token a
genuinely failing subject produces. Those three cost real time this session and none is greppable.

title: Typed completion signal: the worker says done — nothing infers it
description:
WHAT: two missing mechanisms in the dispatch loop, measured together at 22:39:30Z from one tick-monitor payload. Josh named both: "why isn't our crate substrate finding that pane 4 is idle and why isn't pane 4 letting you know when they are done."

FAILURE 1 — THE OBSERVER FINDS IT AND THEN DISCARDS IT. This is worse than blindness.

  raw tmux, %1408:  the pi glyph        -> idle
  tick-monitor, same instant:
      %1408 state=IDLE t=0                              <- the kernel KNOWS
      idle_panes: {dispatchable: [], count: 0, free_capacity: []}   <- and throws it away

The STATE field is correct. The ACTIONABLE field is empty. Any consumer reading `idle_panes` — which is the field a dispatcher would consume — sees no capacity while a pane sits idle. The information exists and is destroyed one layer up.

ROOT CAUSE, already documented in this repo as a FIXED bug: `free_capacity` is derived from the same `is_dispatchable` filter as `dispatchable`, and `dispatchable` requires CONFIRMED idle (two captures >=75s apart). A pane at t=0 is NEWLY idle, so it is excluded from BOTH lists. omp-orchestrator/src/lib.rs:163-166 records the identical defect verbatim: "an earlier version derived both from one filter, which made the NewlyIdle branch of decide unreachable ... the exact shape that let the fleet sit idle while every watchdog reported healthy."

THE FIX LANDED IN omp-orchestrator AND NOT IN tick-monitor — the observer kept the bug the decider removed. Filed as tickmonitor-free-capacity-blind-vgf, still open. This is its THIRD live occurrence today: the 178-tick capacity failure, panes 4 and 5 at 19:22, and %1408 now.

FAILURE 2 — NO COMPLETION SIGNAL EXISTS AT ALL. This one has no bead until now.

%1408 finished its work somewhere between 22:35 and 22:39 and NOTHING TOLD THE CONDUCTOR. There is no worker->conductor "done" path in this system. Every completion this session was discovered by the conductor happening to look, or by a human saying so in chat.

AND THE FOLLOW-UP STAGE DOES NOT CLOSE THIS. `classify_followup` (ack-spine, closed today) detects SILENCE past a deadline — "this pane went quiet and owes a verdict." That is the pathological case. It does not detect COMPLETION — "this worker finished, here is the verdict, the pane is free." A healthy finish and a hang look identical to a silence detector until the deadline expires, which means every clean completion costs a full deadline of idle time before anything notices.

THE CHAIN, AND WHERE EACH LINK STANDS:
  observe        tick-monitor        WORKS (state is correct)
  actionable     idle_panes          BROKEN (vgf) — discards NewlyIdle
  consumer       supervisor decide() FENCED — 162 refused ticks, owner=josh
  actuator       the conductor       A HUMAN-DRIVEN LOOP, ~30 hand dispatches today
  completion     nothing             DOES NOT EXIST
Four links, one works.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. A TYPED COMPLETION SIGNAL, emitted BY THE WORKER, not inferred by a watcher. It carries: bead id, terminal verdict, evidence reference, and the pane's freed-capacity claim. Inference is what we have; it costs a deadline and cannot distinguish finished from wedged.
2. IT MUST SURVIVE PANE DEATH. Per the measured ack analysis, the only artifact that survives a pane dying, a context compaction, and a daemon restart is a durable tracker row. A message is not a completion record. Signal via the bead; the pane may be gone by the time anyone reads it.
3. COMPLETION AND SILENCE ARE DISTINCT OUTCOMES and must not collapse into one enum arm. `Finished{verdict}` and `SilentPastDeadline{minutes}` are different facts with different responses — refill versus investigate. A single "not working" state is the free_capacity defect repeating at a higher layer.
4. FIRES-ON-KNOWN-GOOD: a worker completing normally produces a completion row WITHOUT the conductor polling. Assert the row exists after a real finish. This is the leg that proves the signal is pushed rather than discovered.
5. FIRES-ON-KNOWN-BAD: a worker that dies mid-task produces NO completion row, and the silence detector — not this mechanism — is what fires. Assert the two paths do not overlap.
6. ANTI-VACUITY: zero completions observed in a window where a bead moved to closed is an ERROR. A completion mechanism that never fires is indistinguishable from a fleet that never finishes anything.

DEPENDENCY, STATED HONESTLY: this composes with vgf but does not replace it. Even a perfect completion signal leaves `free_capacity` wrong for panes that go idle WITHOUT completing a bead — an interrupted worker, a cleared pane, a fresh start. Both are needed; neither subsumes the other.

NO-CLAIM 1: a completion signal makes a finish VISIBLE, not VERIFIED. The worker asserts it finished; the conductor still re-runs the cited command before closing. Nine beads today were closed on re-run evidence and two were REFUSED after their author reported success.
NO-CLAIM 2: this closes the notification gap, not the actuation gap. Something must still consume the signal and dispatch. Today that consumer is a human, the supervisor is fenced, and an accurate signal nobody reads is the 178-tick failure with better data.

comments.author: SilverWolf
comments.text:
WAVE .4 DISPATCH — MEASURED VERDICT (SilverWolf, pane 5, %1409). Zero builds. Every claim re-derived from the installed binary at runtime.

THE DECIDING QUESTION ANSWERED: does --mode=rpc expose a send-with-receipt for a pane we do not own? **NO.** OMP's --mode=rpc is a SINGLE-SESSION transport — it speaks to the OMP instance in the current process, not to other panes or sessions. Measured: get_state returns structured model data, but there is no pane management, no cross-session dispatch, and no send-to-third-party capability. The mux* methods (muxConnect/muxPing/muxRestartServer) are for the TUI multiplexing layer, not accessible from --mode=rpc.

CLASSIFICATION CORRECTED FROM THE ORCHESTRATOR'S ORIGINAL:
  pane state      (b)→ MIXED: --mode=rpc get_state provides structured model/session state for OUR OWN session — category (b) is correct for single-session state queries. Cross-pane state still requires tmux capture-pane because OMP's RPC cannot see other sessions. So: (b) for same-session state, (a) for cross-pane state.
  dispatch        (b)→ CORRECTED TO (a): OMP's RPC cannot address a third-party pane. tmux send-keys and ntm robot-send are the ONLY mechanisms that work for cross-pane dispatch. Scraping is correct here — there is no OMP alternative to switch to.
  health check    (b)→ MIXED: omp/muxPing exists but is not accessible from --mode=rpc (the mux* layer is TUI-only). The heartbeat file we write IS the correct mechanism. Category (a) for cross-pane, (b) for own-session state.
  session         (b)→ CONFIRMED: OMP's --continue/--resume/--session-dir are real capabilities we should use instead of pane-id tracking. This is the strongest (b) finding.
  receipt         (b)→ NOT CONFIRMED: OMP's --mode=rpc does not provide a delivery receipt for a sent message. The receiver-verification gap (cp-z42vu) cannot be closed by OMP's RPC layer.

THE 42 HANDLER METHODS CLAIM: I probed the --mode=rpc transport and found it accepts input commands (text, get_state, and others) but I could not enumerate the full method registry. The "42 handler methods" figure from the orchestrator's census is plausible but I could not independently derive the complete list. The RPC mode responds to unknown commands with a typed error, so the method set is discoverable by probing — but a comprehensive enumeration requires running a live OMP session with real work, which is beyond this grading pass.

WAVE .4 SURFACES CLASSIFIED:
  irc          (a) genuinely not ours
  collab       (c) capability we should use — multi-agent coordination in OMP
  jsonrpc      (a) genuinely not ours — LSP/DAP message framing, not orchestration
  mcp          (a) genuinely not ours
  launch       (c) capability we should use — OMP's launch/launchd integration
  exec         (b) we reimplemented via subprocess — OMP's exec surface provides structured tool execution
  subprocess   (a) genuinely not ours — OMP internal subprocess management

NO-CLAIM: the --mode=rpc probes ran against a no-session, no-tools, no-lsp, no-extensions instance. A production OMP session with extensions and LSP would expose a different (likely larger) RPC surface. The classification is correct for the launched configuration tested.
